These bounds are controlled by the distance of the normalized density profile from the Poincar\'e density manifold times the number of particles. In particular, these bounds show that the TFW approximation is exact on the Poincar\'e manifold. We then show that, in the periodic setting, the distance between the Kohn-Sham potential and the inverse TFW potential in the natural dual Sobolev space can also be controlled by explicit density dependent constants times the distance to the Poincar\'e manifold. As a corollary, we prove that for a fixed density profile, the Kohn-Sham potential converges towards the inverse Thomas--Fermi potential in the high-density limit [MATH] with asymptotic rate of order [MATH]. This rate is shown to be optimal.
tldr: The paper proves a sharp one-dimensional Lieb-Thirring inequality with gradient correction and applies it to bound errors of the Thomas-Fermi-von Weizsäcker kinetic-energy approximation in density functional theory.
motivation: Lieb-Thirring-type bounds and their sharp constants are central to controlling kinetic energy functionals, and the accuracy of the TFW approximation in DFT lacks explicit non-asymptotic error bounds.
method: Rigorous functional and spectral analysis: derivation of a sharp inequality with semiclassical constant plus gradient and parity-dependent shell corrections in the periodic setting, characterization of optimizers forming a 'Poincaré density manifold', and dual Sobolev-space estimates on the Kohn-Sham potential.
result: Explicit non-asymptotic global and local error bounds for the TFW approximation controlled by the distance of the density to the Poincaré manifold, exactness on that manifold, and an optimal high-density convergence rate of the Kohn-Sham potential to the inverse Thomas-Fermi potential for fixed density profiles.
conclusion: The work provides sharp analytical tools for quantifying the accuracy of semiclassical kinetic-energy functionals, but remains within mathematical density functional theory rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Scaling Local Solvers With The Many-Body Expansion
authors: Federico Zahariev (iowa State University, Ames Laboratory), Amr Sabry
abstract: ArXiv:2610.30137v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce a Many-Body Expansion framework for scaling black-box solvers for discrete optimization. The method decomposes a large problem into fragments, repeatedly improves each fragment with the rest of the assignment held fixed, and then applies targeted corrections on unions of fragments. The solver itself is unchanged: it only receives a restricted subproblem and returns a candidate assignment. The framework separates decomposition from solver design. Moebius inversion gives an exact fragment expansion of the objective, and for pairwise objectives such as graph coloring, MAX-CUT, and QUBO the expansion closes at second order. The promoted solver is monotone by construction, terminates in finitely many productive sweeps for non-negative integer-valued objectives, and connects to junction-tree dynamic programming when the fragment interaction structure is acyclic and full response functions are propagated. On graph coloring benchmarks, the promoted versions of TabuSearch and simulated annealing (SA) generally outperform flat applications of the same solvers, often finding better solutions in less CPU time, and the gain proves insensitive to the choice of graph partition. A facility-location study delimits the claim: there the partition must respect the objective's interaction locality, and the promoted solver reaches within 0.3-1.4% of GLPK-certified optima at every tested size. The same wrapper interface is used in each solver-swap case, and the facility-location check reuses the same monotone guard with a sign-adjusted interaction diagnostic; the improvements therefore come from the MBE promotion mechanism rather than solver-specific tuning.
tldr: A Many-Body Expansion framework that wraps black-box discrete-optimization solvers, decomposing problems into fragments and applying Möbius-inversion-based corrections to improve solution quality.
motivation: Large discrete optimization problems (graph coloring, MAX-CUT, QUBO) are hard for monolithic solvers, and the authors want a decomposition wrapper that improves any solver without modifying it.
method: The objective is expanded exactly via Möbius inversion over fragments; the solver is repeatedly applied to restricted subproblems with the remaining assignment fixed, followed by targeted corrections on fragment unions, giving a monotone promoted solver that terminates in finitely many productive sweeps.
result: Promoted TabuSearch and simulated annealing outperform their flat counterparts on graph-coloring benchmarks with insensitivity to partitioning, and on facility location reach within 0.3–1.4% of GLPK-certified optima.
conclusion: The MBE promotion mechanism yields solver-agnostic gains, though partitioning must respect the objective's interaction locality for problems like facility location.

title: Strongly Regular Graph Construction Via Quadratic Binary Optimization
authors: D. Osorio, P. Andagana, V. Gonz\'alez, J. Czartowski, D. Goyeneche
abstract: ArXiv:2610.30142v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Strongly regular graphs, hereafter SRGs, are highly structured combinatorial objects of central interest in algebraic graph theory and quantum information, whose explicit construction becomes rapidly intractable as the number of vertices grows; Conway's still unresolved [MATH]-graph problem is an emblematic example. The matrix equation defining SRGs is quadratic in the binary edge variables, so the natural penalty enforcing it, a sum of squared residuals, is quartic and lies outside quadratic unconstrained binary optimization, known as QUBO. We prove a considerably stronger obstruction, namely that no quadratic function of the edge variables has the labeled SRGs as its exact set of global minimizers, except for three degenerate families given by the perfect matchings, the cocktail-party graphs and the pentagon. In particular, we formally establish that the [MATH]-vertex graph of Conway's problem cannot be obtained from any QUBO over the edge variables without auxiliary variables. Guided by this theorem we develop two complementary algorithms. The first operates within pure QUBO, solves the degenerate families exactly, and beyond them works as a generate--prune--verify pipeline whose output is a reduced set of candidates certified by a polynomial-time classical test. The second solves the full problem by quadratizing this quartic penalty through Rosenberg auxiliary variables, whose number grows as [MATH] with the number of vertices [MATH]. We test the pure-QUBO route under simulated annealing on all feasible families with at most [MATH] vertices and the auxiliary-variable route on representative targets up to [MATH] vertices, and tabulate the algebraically feasible parameter sets for graphs with at most [MATH] vertices.
tldr: The paper studies constructing strongly regular graphs using quadratic binary optimization, proving limitations of pure QUBO formulations and proposing auxiliary-variable and generate-prune-verify approaches.
motivation: Strongly regular graphs are important combinatorial objects whose explicit construction becomes intractable as the number of vertices grows, with Conway's graph problem as a notable open case.
method: The authors prove that no quadratic function of edge variables can exactly characterize labeled strongly regular graphs except for three degenerate families, then develop a pure-QUBO generate-prune-verify pipeline and a Rosenberg auxiliary-variable quadratization scheme.
result: They test the pure-QUBO route with simulated annealing on feasible families up to a small number of vertices and the auxiliary-variable route on representative targets up to larger sizes, while tabulating algebraically feasible parameter sets.
conclusion: Pure QUBO is insufficient for general strongly regular graph construction without auxiliary variables, but hybrid QUBO and quadratization approaches can handle restricted and larger cases.

title: A Reciprocal Graph-deviation Functional: Structural Identifiability From Controlled Equilibrium Maps
authors: Megan Simons Jonathan Washburn
abstract: ArXiv:2610.30146v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We constructed a reciprocal graph-deviation functional for positive ratios on a finite weighted graph. Its scalar generator [MATH] was characterized previously by ratio-composition and unit log-curvature. Our principal new result was structural identifiability: already on a two-site, one-edge system, the complete minimizer-location map obtained by sweeping the boundary and site-to-edge weight ratio determines any reciprocal generator whose log-coordinate representation is [MATH] with everywhere-positive curvature, up to a positive scale; unit-curvature calibration fixes that scale. For the calibrated reciprocal family~[MATH] we obtained the equilibrium response in closed form. A synthetic [MATH]-condition sweep with seven simulated measurements per condition and log-scale noise [MATH] selected [MATH] over~[MATH] with probability~[MATH] under exact boundary and weight parameters; a declared representation-uncertainty screen lowered that value to approximately~[MATH]. These probabilities characterize the simulated design under the declared data-generating model. The finite sweep discriminated prespecified generators, whereas nonparametric recovery required the complete response map. We also recorded the associated convex gradient-flow and Langevin dynamics.
tldr: The paper introduces a reciprocal graph-deviation functional on finite weighted graphs and studies structural identifiability of its generator from controlled equilibrium response maps.
motivation: The authors aim to characterize when a reciprocal generator can be uniquely recovered from observed equilibrium behavior on a simple two-site graph.
method: They analyze a minimizer-location map generated by sweeping boundary and site-to-edge weight ratios, prove identifiability up to scale, calibrate via unit curvature, and perform a synthetic condition sweep with simulated noisy measurements.
result: The complete equilibrium response map identifies any positive-curvature reciprocal generator up to positive scale, and the calibrated family yields closed-form equilibrium response; simulations favor a specific generator with high probability under the stated model.
conclusion: Structural identifiability requires the full response map rather than finite sweeps, and the framework connects to convex gradient-flow and Langevin dynamics.

title: Partial Breakdown Of Integrability In Nearly Integrable Systems
authors: Shoya Motonaga Marian Gidea
abstract: ArXiv:2610.30354v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the persistence of integrable structures in real-analytic nearly integrable systems under perturbations that may destroy some, but not all, of these structures. Specifically, we establish upper bounds on the numbers of real-analytic first integrals -- quantities conserved by the motion -- and commuting vector fields -- infinitesimal generators of continuous symmetries -- that can persist under the perturbation. These bounds are expressed in terms of Melnikov-type functions, which quantify the breakdown of the corresponding integrable structures. Unlike classical Melnikov theory, our conditions occur even in the absence of zeros of the Melnikov functions, so they do not necessarily imply the existence of homoclinic tangles. We give a geometric interpretation of these conditions in the context of the Arnold diffusion problem, showing that they imply micro-diffusion. We also obtain a criterion for higher-dimensional nearly integrable systems in which the dimension of the span of the Melnikov vectors restricts the numbers of possible first integrals and commuting vector fields. This shows that the geometry of the Melnikov vectors provides a new mechanism for detecting the breakdown of integrability. We give several applications to integrable Hamiltonian systems subject to forcing and dissipation.
tldr: The paper derives upper bounds on the persistence of first integrals and commuting vector fields in nearly integrable real-analytic Hamiltonian systems using Melnikov-type functions.
motivation: It aims to understand how perturbations partially destroy integrable structures in nearly integrable systems and to characterize this breakdown geometrically, including connections to Arnold diffusion.
method: The authors use Melnikov-type functions and geometric criteria involving the span of Melnikov vectors to bound the number of surviving real-analytic first integrals and commuting vector fields.
result: The main results give upper bounds on persisting integrable structures even without zeros of the Melnikov functions, imply micro-diffusion in the Arnold diffusion context, and provide a higher-dimensional criterion based on the geometry of Melnikov vectors.
conclusion: The geometry of Melnikov vectors offers a new mechanism for detecting partial breakdown of integrability, with applications to forced and dissipative integrable Hamiltonian systems.

title: HAWC-Leak: Heterogeneous Architecture Workload Classification Utilizing Side-Channel Leakage
authors: Muhtasim Alam Chowdhury, Arthur Kim, Rozhin Yasaei, Soheil Salehi
abstract: ArXiv:2610.30400v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Modern heterogeneous computing platforms, which integrate general-purpose processors with specialized accelerators such as FPGAs, have become the standard for high-performance and embedded applications. However, the shared physical resources of these systems introduce critical security vulnerabilities, where power consumption patterns can leak sensitive runtime information. While side-channel analysis is well established for extracting cryptographic keys from isolated algorithms, existing methods struggle to profile complex, dynamic systems where diverse workloads coexist on shared hardware resources. This paper presents HAWC-Leak, a dynamic workload classification framework designed to identify specific hardware accelerator tasks in real time using non-invasive power analysis. Unlike prior studies focused on extracting cryptographic secrets from isolated implementations, our approach profiles heterogeneous runtime behavior using machine learning to predict active workloads from features extracted from power traces. We implement a complete hardware-in-the-loop measurement testbed using the ChipWhisperer CW305 Artix-7 FPGA platform to capture high-resolution power signatures of diverse workloads including Advanced Encryption Standard (AES-128), Elliptic Curve Cryptography (ECC P-256), Secure Hash Algorithm (SHA-256), Convolutional Neural Network (CNN), and a system idle state. We develop a Hierarchical Random Forest classifier that processes real-time power data to identify the executing application in controlled mixed-activity scenarios where multiple accelerators are instantiated but only one executes at a time. Experimental results demonstrate that this framework achieves 100% classification accuracy across all evaluated scenarios, confirming that power consumption patterns serve as a reliable and distinctive fingerprint for profiling heterogeneous runtime behavior.
tldr: HAWC-Leak uses machine-learning classification of power side-channel traces to identify which accelerator workload (AES, ECC, SHA, CNN, or idle) is executing on a heterogeneous FPGA-based platform.
motivation: Heterogeneous platforms sharing physical resources leak runtime information through power consumption, but existing side-channel methods are designed for isolated cryptographic implementations and cannot profile complex systems with multiple coexisting workloads.
method: The authors build a hardware-in-the-loop testbed on the ChipWhisperer CW305 Artix-7 FPGA, capture high-resolution power traces for five workloads, extract features, and train a hierarchical random forest classifier for real-time identification.
result: The framework reports 100% classification accuracy across all evaluated mixed-activity scenarios where a single accelerator executes at a time.
conclusion: Power signatures are a reliable fingerprint for profiling heterogeneous runtime behavior, enabling non-invasive workload monitoring, though the work is classical hardware security with no quantum information, thermodynamic, network, or hybrid-quantum-system content.

title: Alexander Torsion And Floer Comparisons In The Bv-bfv Formalism
authors: Nima Moshayedi
abstract: ArXiv:2610.30192v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We compare relative Abelian BF torsion with the Alexander-graded Euler characteristic of knot Floer homology. A meridional annulus boundary condition identifies the normalized relative torsion with the Alexander polynomial. One exact prime-cyclotomic torsion value recovers all its coefficients under a sharp genus bound, compatibly with connected-sum gluing and branched-cover formulas. We compute interface contractions and obstructions to scalar comparisons, including the pairing defect of two-sector reduction for the degree-zero torus algebra. A six-generator dg resolution yields an equivalence of perfect-module categories preserving derived pairings and admits a classical one-dimensional BV-BFV realization. In the fixed nonresonant polynomial quantum BFV sector, over characteristic zero with [MATH] inverted, both states and Weyl observables reduce to a vacuum field; a Hochschild invariant obstructs a Morita equivalence with the degree-zero torus algebra. These results do not establish a full geometric BV-BFV/Floer equivalence.
tldr: The paper compares relative Abelian BF torsion with the Alexander-graded Euler characteristic of knot Floer homology within the BV-BFV formalism, computing interface contractions and obstructions to scalar comparisons.
motivation: The author aims to relate torsion invariants from Abelian BF theory to knot Floer homology data, and to probe how far a BV-BFV formulation can reproduce Floer-theoretic structures.
method: Relative Abelian BF torsion is computed under a meridional annulus boundary condition, normalized, and matched against the Alexander polynomial; interface contractions, a six-generator dg resolution, and a fixed nonresonant polynomial quantum BFV sector are analyzed.
result: The normalized relative torsion reproduces the Alexander polynomial (with a prime-cyclotomic value recovering all coefficients under a genus bound), a six-generator resolution yields an equivalence of perfect-module categories, and a Hochschild invariant obstructs Morita equivalence with the degree-zero torus algebra.
conclusion: The results clarify partial correspondences and obstructions but explicitly do not establish a full geometric BV-BFV/Floer equivalence.

title: Black-Hole Ringdown From Photon-Sphere Modes In An Elastic Analogue
authors: Jiaoqing Wang, Chenni Xu, Sophia Purow, S\'ebastien Guenneau, Patrick Sebbah
abstract: ArXiv:2610.30396v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quasinormal modes (QNMs) govern the ringdown of black holes, yet their physical origin and experimental accessibility remain limited. Here we create an elastic analogue of a black hole using a curved metallic shell engineered to emulate a Schwarzschild-like metric, and directly probe its vibrational dynamics in the time domain. Following impulsive excitation, the elastic system exhibits a clear ringdown response, providing a tangible analogue of black-hole ringing. The underlying modes are flexural vibrations localized near the photon sphere. A reduction of the thin-shell elastic equations yields a photon-sphere effective potential and predicts the dependence of the localized-mode frequencies on azimuthal order. Crucially, they persist even when boundary reflections are strongly suppressed, demonstrating that their confinement is governed by a curvature-induced effective potential rather than by cavity boundaries. This platform enables direct access to quasinormal modes through both their temporal decay and spectral signatures, establishing a direct connection between photon-sphere dynamics and ringdown. More broadly, our results identify curvature-induced trapping as a general mechanism for wave localization and dissipation in open systems.
tldr: An elastic analogue of a Schwarzschild black hole built from a curved metallic shell reproduces black-hole ringdown via flexural modes trapped by a photon-sphere effective potential.
motivation: Quasinormal modes govern black-hole ringdown, but their physical origin and experimental accessibility remain limited, motivating tabletop analogues that make the dynamics directly observable.
method: A curved thin metallic shell is engineered to emulate a Schwarzschild-like metric and impulsively excited, with time-domain vibrational measurements compared against a reduced photon-sphere effective-potential model for thin-shell elasticity.
result: The system exhibits a clear ringdown with localized flexural modes whose frequencies follow the predicted azimuthal-order dependence, and these modes persist even when boundary reflections are strongly suppressed.
conclusion: Confinement is due to curvature-induced effective potential rather than cavity boundaries, establishing curvature-induced trapping as a general mechanism for wave localization and dissipation in open systems.

title: Metasurface Engineering Of Transient Photothermal Responses For Vibrational Imaging At Living Interfaces
authors: Zhibin Hu, Tianrun Zhang, Jiayu Ding, Pengcheng Fu, Ziyang Huang, Bo Chen, Bangjie Song, Minglu Li, Xinyu Deng, Quan D. Zhou, Delong Zhang, Siying Peng
abstract: ArXiv:2610.30610v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Chemical transformations at biological interfaces are central to cellular function, yet the weak vibrational signals associated with subtle molecular changes limit their spatially resolved observation. Here, we present metasurface-driven mid-infrared photothermal imaging (MetaMIP), which uses resonantly engineered metasurfaces to amplify molecular temperature modulation while retaining rapid thermal recovery. Visible-light detection converts this response into submicrometre maps of individual nanoparticles and biological cells. In living cells, MetaMIP resolves spatially distinct chemical changes during enzymatic lipid conversion across the cell membrane. These results demonstrate the potential of engineered photothermal interfaces for mapping chemical composition and tracking its evolution during reactions.
tldr: The paper introduces MetaMIP, a metasurface-enhanced mid-infrared photothermal imaging method for submicrometre vibrational mapping of chemical changes at living biological interfaces.
motivation: Weak vibrational signals from subtle molecular changes at biological interfaces are difficult to observe with spatial resolution, motivating resonant metasurface engineering to amplify photothermal response.
method: Resonantly engineered metasurfaces amplify mid-infrared molecular temperature modulation while allowing rapid thermal recovery; visible-light detection converts this into submicrometre chemical maps of nanoparticles and living cells.
result: MetaMIP resolves individual nanoparticles and spatially distinct chemical changes during enzymatic lipid conversion across living cell membranes.
conclusion: Engineered photothermal interfaces enable label-free mapping of chemical composition and reaction evolution at biological interfaces, with potential for live-cell chemical imaging.

title: Intrinsic Angular Momentum Contribution To The Sagnac Response Of A Rotating Helical Optical Fiber
authors: Lili Yang, Pengming Zhang, Longlong Feng
abstract: ArXiv:2610.30898v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate rotation-induced phase accumulation of structured light in a mechanically rotating uniform helical optical fiber using a four-component optical Dirac-like equation. In the paraxial and weak-geometry regime, the intrinsic dynamics contain a torsion-induced geometric coupling and a mechanical rotation--angular-momentum coupling. We show that, in a common-path mirror-reflection geometry, both the torsion-induced geometric phase and the conventional area-dependent Sagnac contribution cancel over a complete round trip, whereas the intrinsic rotation--angular-momentum phase survives. The surviving phase depends on the intrinsic total angular momentum of the structured optical mode and provides a common-path interferometric route for probing intrinsic angular momentum effects in rotational sensing.
tldr: The paper analyzes rotation-induced phase accumulation of structured light in a helical optical fiber and identifies an intrinsic rotation-angular-momentum phase that survives common-path cancellation.
motivation: The authors aim to isolate intrinsic angular-momentum effects in rotational sensing using a common-path interferometric geometry where conventional Sagnac and torsion-induced geometric phases cancel.
method: They use a four-component optical Dirac-like equation in the paraxial and weak-geometry regime to derive the phase contributions for structured light in a mechanically rotating uniform helical fiber.
result: Over a complete round trip in a mirror-reflection geometry, the torsion-induced geometric phase and area-dependent Sagnac contribution cancel, while the intrinsic rotation-angular-momentum phase remains and depends on the mode's total angular momentum.
conclusion: The surviving phase offers a common-path interferometric route for probing intrinsic angular momentum effects in rotational sensing, but the work is classical/optical sensing rather than quantum information.

title: Learning Cole-Hopf Coordinates For Stochastic Growth Dynamics: The Kpz Class
authors: Lorenzo Mensi, Simone Cuonzo, Maria Chiara Angelini, Sergio Chibbaro, Cyril Furtlehner, Alberto Rosso
abstract: ArXiv:2610.30919v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Inferring effective equations from observations of nonlinear stochastic processes is challenging because individual trajectories are noisy realizations, while the relevant physical information is encoded in ensemble statistics. We introduce a data-driven framework that learns a change of variables in which nonlinear stochastic dynamics become linear. The model combines a neural change of representation with a linear stochastic latent evolution and is trained through a short-time moment-matching objective, thereby avoiding trajectory during optimization. This construction yields an interpretable generative model: both the learned transformation and the latent evolution operators can be directly inspected. We validate the method on the one-dimensional Kardar--Parisi--Zhang (KPZ) equation, a paradigmatic model of stochastic growth for which the Cole--Hopf transformation maps the nonlinear dynamics to the stochastic heat equation. From simulated height trajectories alone, the model recovers the local exponential Cole--Hopf map and the associated linear stochastic operator. Generated trajectories reproduce the main statistical signatures of the KPZ universality class, including the growth law [MATH] with [MATH] and the GOE Tracy--Widom height distribution for flat initial conditions. These results show that interpretable stochastic equations can be inferred from data by learning representations in which the dynamics closes in a simple form. Furthermore the development of the physical informed learning permits to get insights on the physics of the dynamical process.
tldr: A data-driven neural framework learns a change of variables (Cole-Hopf coordinates) that linearizes nonlinear stochastic growth dynamics, validated on the 1D KPZ equation.
motivation: Inferring effective stochastic equations from noisy trajectories is hard because physical content lives in ensemble statistics rather than individual realizations.
method: The authors combine a neural change of representation with a linear stochastic latent evolution, trained via a short-time moment-matching objective that avoids trajectory matching during optimization.
result: From simulated height trajectories alone, the model recovers the local exponential Cole-Hopf map and linear stochastic operator, reproducing KPZ scaling (growth exponent) and GOE Tracy-Widom statistics for flat initial conditions.
conclusion: Interpretable stochastic equations can be inferred by learning representations in which the dynamics closes in a simple linear form, offering physics-informed insight into universality classes.

title: Active Phase Separation From Concentration-dependent Diffusion In Chemical Networks
authors: Ramin Golestanian Giulia Pisegna
abstract: ArXiv:2610.30958v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Active phase separation in living systems is ubiquitous, yet the microscopic origins of the non-equilibrium terms in active field theories remain largely unknown. Here, starting from stochastic mass-conserving reaction-diffusion dynamics of two interacting chemical species, we perform a systematic slow-mode reduction and derive the complete Active Model B+ field theory, with all phenomenological coefficients expressed in terms of microscopic parameters. We identify concentration-dependent diffusivities and asymmetric inter-species chemotactic couplings as the minimal microscopic ingredients generating the genuinely non-equilibrium coefficient responsible for microphase separation, cluster phases, and arrested coarsening. Our framework recovers the equilibrium limit consistently and is validated by stochastic numerical simulations. These results establish a direct, bottom-up link between the architecture of chemical reaction networks and the universality class of their emergent large-scale dynamics.
tldr: A systematic slow-mode reduction of stochastic mass-conserving reaction-diffusion dynamics for two interacting chemical species derives the full Active Model B+ field theory with microscopically expressed coefficients.
motivation: The microscopic origins of non-equilibrium terms in active field theories for active phase separation remain largely unknown, motivating a bottom-up derivation from chemical reaction network architecture.
method: Starting from stochastic mass-conserving reaction-diffusion dynamics of two interacting species, the authors perform a systematic slow-mode (coarse-graining) reduction and validate the resulting field theory with stochastic numerical simulations.
result: Concentration-dependent diffusivities and asymmetric inter-species chemotactic couplings are identified as the minimal microscopic ingredients generating the genuinely non-equilibrium term responsible for microphase separation, cluster phases, and arrested coarsening, with the equilibrium limit recovered consistently.
conclusion: The work establishes a direct bottom-up link between the architecture of chemical reaction networks and the universality class of their emergent large-scale dynamics.

title: The Smfce Paradigm: A Unified Modeling Framework Based On State, Cost, And Extremal Evolution
authors: Wei Ba, Ang Fu, Shengsong Kong, Zhongchuan Fu
abstract: ArXiv:2610.30140v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper proposes a unified modeling framework centered on "state-cost-extremal evolution," referred to as the SMFCE paradigm. The paradigm represents the effective state of a system as a point in a state space, characterizes state cost by a single-valued scalar field, and describes system evolution through local cost descent or local extremum selection. Its mathematical core employs classical tools from differential geometry, gradient systems, and dynamical systems. The contribution of this paper is not to reintroduce these foundational results, but to organize them into two operational modeling principles. On finite-dimensional smooth Riemannian manifolds under appropriate regularity conditions, the path independence of cost differences and the cost monotonicity of negative gradient flows follow directly from classical results, while the descent property of discrete local-minimum transitions follows directly from the definition of a minimum. For same-level iterative emergence and present-centeredness, the paper provides conditional mathematical formulations using, respectively, parameterized gradient systems and bifurcation theory, and Markov processes and receding-horizon optimization. The paper further introduces three layered metrics: cost quantity, directed coupling degree, and commitment fulfillment rate, at the state, transition, path, and system levels. Finally, the paper discusses semantic modeling of large language model training and inference within this framework, explicitly distinguishes classical mathematical results, conditional propositions, and empirical adaptation models, and provides reproducible empirical testing procedures for the two modeling principles.
tldr: The paper proposes a generic 'state–cost–extremal evolution' (SMFCE) modeling paradigm built from classical differential geometry, gradient systems, and dynamical systems theory, illustrated with speculative applications to LLM training and inference.
motivation: The authors aim to unify diverse modeling approaches by organizing well-known mathematical tools into two operational modeling principles (path-independent cost differences / cost-monotone gradient descent), motivated by a desire for a general descriptive language for complex systems including large language models.
method: The framework represents system states as points on Riemannian manifolds, defines a scalar cost field, and describes evolution via negative gradient flows, discrete local-minimum transitions, parameterized gradient systems, bifurcation theory, and receding-horizon optimization; three layered metrics (cost quantity, directed coupling degree, commitment fulfillment rate) are introduced.
result: The claimed properties—path independence of cost differences, cost monotonicity of negative gradient flows, and descent of discrete local-minimum transitions—are shown to follow directly from standard classical results; other features (same-level iterative emergence, present-centeredness) are given only conditional formulations, and the LLM discussion is explicitly labeled as semantic/empirical adaptation rather than derived.
conclusion: The work is a conceptual meta-framework restating classical mathematical facts with no quantum information, quantum thermodynamics, networking, or hybrid-systems content; its scientific value for the stated research interests is negligible.

title: Elimination Geometry Ii: Integrability, Representation, And Structural Limits
authors: Xueqin Wang Mian Huang
abstract: ArXiv:2610.30145v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Elimination geometry studies the exact nonnegative defect left after an auxiliary variable is optimized out. Part~II audits this certified-elimination interface through three theorem families. For integrability, local gaps form a repeated partial-elimination tower precisely under nonnegativity, touching, and zero elementary-square circulation. Hodge projection constructs nearest finite-space repairs and separates curvature, certification, and global period taxes. For representation and price, a descent gate characterizes surjective refinements and rules out strictly convex separable, duplication-invariant weight penalties. Dummy and target-calling lifts show that unrestricted lift design is vacuous, whereas the Fidelity-coherence frontier isolates irreducible cost. A modal Gram block classifies unconstrained quadratic lift-coupling germs and yields aligned Gaussian risk ledgers. Bernstein spectral functions preserve graph-Laplacian structure. Graph-universal Markov resolvents exist exactly up to first-order fractional qualification, and universal polynomial spectral penalties reduce to nonnegative Laplacian multiples. This linear limit does not preclude Part~I's nonlinear CDF repair and sharp CRPS theory. For converses, finite-order target-jet preservation uniquely requires subtraction of the corresponding defect jet, up to flat terms; approximate jets yield quasi-descent and stationary limits. Fixed-marginal coupling obeys a dependence-benefit frontier. Reversing certified KL in entropy-regularized control eliminates dimension-free guarantees, while a fixed measurement preserves all Umegaki defects of a faithful Gibbs family exactly when that family commutes.
tldr: This paper develops an elimination-geometry framework for certified optimization and representation, with structural theorems on integrability, convex penalties, graph-Laplacian spectral forms, and entropy-regularized control.
motivation: The work aims to audit the interface left after auxiliary variables are eliminated, characterizing exact nonnegative defects and the limits of lift-based representations and penalized objectives.
method: It proves three families of theorems using partial-elimination towers, Hodge projection, descent gates, modal Gram blocks, Bernstein spectral functions, and converses for target-jet preservation and KL-regularized control.
result: The paper shows that unrestricted lift design is vacuous, universal polynomial spectral penalties reduce to nonnegative Laplacian multiples, and reversing certified KL in entropy-regularized control destroys dimension-free guarantees.
conclusion: The framework isolates irreducible costs and structural limits in elimination-based optimization, with only tangential connections to quantum information via Umegaki relative entropy and Gibbs families.

title: The Gittins Index For A Transparent One-Armed Bandit With A Continuous Payoff Spectrum In Equilibrium States
authors: Marcin Makowski, Edward W. Piotrowski, Jan L. Cie\'sli\'nski
abstract: ArXiv:2610.30150v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present an analogue of the classical Gittins index for a one-armed decision problem with a continuous spectrum of payoffs. The model assumes that the decision-maker observes independent realizations of a random variable and, at each step, decides whether to accept the current opportunity or continue observing. We show that the optimal strategy takes the form of a threshold rule, while the corresponding reservation index is determined by a one-dimensional fixed-point equation with a direct decision-theoretic interpretation. The model is illustrated with an example of bookmaker betting related to horse racing and the Kelly criterion. This perspective allows the proposed index to be viewed as a threshold of informational advantage. This, in turn, points to potential applications in optimal stopping problems and decision-making under uncertainty.
tldr: The paper derives a Gittins-type index for a transparent one-armed bandit with a continuous payoff spectrum, showing optimal behavior is a threshold rule defined by a one-dimensional fixed-point equation.
motivation: Classical Gittins indices apply to discrete multi-armed bandit problems; the authors seek an analogue for settings with continuous payoff spectra and observable opportunity streams, motivated by betting and optimal stopping scenarios.
method: They formulate a sequential decision problem where a decision-maker observes i.i.d. realizations of a random variable and chooses between accepting the current offer or continuing, then derive the optimal threshold strategy and reservation index via a fixed-point equation.
result: The optimal policy is a threshold rule whose reservation index solves a one-dimensional fixed-point equation with a direct decision-theoretic interpretation, illustrated by horse-race bookmaker betting linked to the Kelly criterion.
conclusion: The index can be interpreted as a threshold of informational advantage, suggesting applications to optimal stopping and decision-making under uncertainty.

title: Triple Products Of Correlated Multivariate Hermite Polynomials
authors: Laura Lyman
abstract: ArXiv:2610.30204v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Stochastic Galerkin schemes (SGS) are used to approximate solutions to differential equations with stochastic parameters. In particular, they express the solution with an infinite orthogonal functional basis of the parameter space and derive a deterministic system of PDEs; the solution of this deterministic system can be used to produce a {surrogate} approximation of the original stochastic equations. When the parameters are correlated, the infinite series representation of the solution does not provably converge for all joint distributions; further, classic decorrelating transformations (e.g., Roseblatt) often introduce known numerical instabilities. Rahman (2017) established convergence in probability and distribution for correlated {Gaussian} parameters when the basis functionals are {multivariate Hermite polynomials} (MHPs), where these polynomials are only {weakly orthogonal} with respect to the underlying joint density. Due to weak orthogonality, the [MATH]th moments of MHPs introduced during Galerkin projection do not trivially decompose into products of one-dimensional expectations and have no closed-form expression for [MATH]; consequently, these moments are typically estimated via brute-force sampling and quickly become prohibitively expensive to compute. In this paper, we introduce and prove several foundational results for MHPs. These results culminate in an equation that can be used to calculate the [MATH] moments (triple products) exactly, whose implementation dramatically reduces the computational bottleneck otherwise inherent to SGS with correlated Gaussian parameters.
tldr: The paper derives exact closed-form expressions for triple products (third moments) of correlated multivariate Hermite polynomials, removing a major computational bottleneck in stochastic Galerkin schemes for correlated Gaussian parameters.
motivation: Stochastic Galerkin schemes with correlated Gaussian parameters rely on weakly orthogonal multivariate Hermite polynomials, whose Galerkin-projection moments cannot be decomposed into products of one-dimensional expectations and are therefore computed by prohibitively expensive brute-force sampling.
method: The author proves several foundational results on multivariate Hermite polynomials and combines them into an explicit equation for the triple-product moments under correlated Gaussian joint densities.
result: An exact, implementable formula for the triple products is obtained, which replaces sampling-based estimation and dramatically reduces the computational cost of the Galerkin projection step.
conclusion: The results make stochastic Galerkin surrogates practical for correlated Gaussian parameters, though the work is purely numerical/applied mathematics with no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum platforms.

title: On The Adversarial Vulnerability Of Neural Receivers With Unrolled Ldpc Decoders
authors: Aakash Saini, Jafar Aco Mohammadi, Wolfgang Gerstacker
abstract: ArXiv:2610.30345v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Neural receivers for 5G New Radio (NR) match classical model-based receivers in link-level performance, but their robustness to adversarial perturbations at the receiver input remains underexplored. We show that standard gradient-based attacks applied end-to-end through an unrolled low-density parity-check (LDPC) decoder fail to significantly outperform a matched-power Gaussian perturbation. We identify the failure as gradient masking caused by tanh saturation in the boxplus operation of the belief-propagation (BP) check-node update, with a per-iteration gradient norm decay of more than four orders of magnitude across ten unrolled BP iterations. Based on this finding, we propose two structurally independent loss functions that restore attack efficacy. L_BP routes the gradient through the unsaturated early iterations via per-iteration supervision, while L_LLR is a margin loss on pre-decoder log-likelihood ratios (LLRs) whose gradient bypasses the LDPC decoder entirely. Both loss functions increase the block-error rate (BLER) by one to four orders of magnitude at matched perturbation power, with the results reproduced on both the Sionna NeuralReceiver and DeepRx. At low PSR, L_LLR-optimized perturbations achieve up to three orders of magnitude higher BLER on unseen channel realizations than LBP-optimized perturbations.
tldr: The paper demonstrates that gradient-based adversarial attacks on neural receivers with unrolled LDPC decoders are hampered by gradient masking from tanh saturation, and proposes two loss functions that restore attack effectiveness by one to four orders of magnitude in BLER.
motivation: Neural receivers for 5G NR match classical receivers in link-level performance, but their robustness to adversarial perturbations at the input is largely unexplored, and naive end-to-end attacks appear to fail.
method: After diagnosing the failure as vanishing per-iteration gradients through the boxplus check-node update of belief propagation, the authors introduce L_BP, which supervises early unsaturated iterations, and L_LLR, a margin loss on pre-decoder LLRs whose gradient bypasses the decoder entirely.
result: Both losses raise block-error rate by one to four orders of magnitude at matched perturbation power on Sionna NeuralReceiver and DeepRx, and L_LLR-optimized perturbations yield up to three orders of magnitude higher BLER than LBP-based ones on unseen channel realizations at low PSR.
conclusion: Gradient masking in unrolled decoders must be addressed explicitly for meaningful adversarial evaluation, and decoder-bypassing losses provide a more transferable attack for neural receiver robustness testing.

title: Comb Tensor Network Finite-Difference Time-Domain Algorithms For 2d And 3d Electromagnetic Simulations
authors: Jonathan Tabares, Erika Ye, Yang Liu
abstract: ArXiv:2610.30486v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper presents efficient 2D and 3D finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) algorithms augmented by the comb tensor network (CTN) representation of the field and auxiliary quantities. The proposed CTN-FDTD algorithm leverages superior compressibility of CTN compared with quantized tensor train (QTT), and rank-reduction strategies including local and global smoothing techniques to achieve logarithmic memory requirement and computation (per time step) cost. Numerical examples validate these complexities and demonstrate the applicability of CTN-FDTD using a variety of source excitation, frequency and permittivity profiles in both 2D and 3D. Remarkably, CTN-FDTD can simulate 35 trillion spatial grid points in 3D with low memory and computation costs on one computation node, whereas standard FDTD would require 281 TB memory to store each of its 31 3D arrays. Moreover, CTN-FDTD was applied to realistic 2D photonic crystal structure simulation with one million grid points and 3D scattering analysis with 8.6 billion grid points.
tldr: The paper introduces comb tensor network (CTN) augmented FDTD algorithms for 2D and 3D electromagnetic simulations achieving logarithmic memory and per-step computational cost.
motivation: Standard FDTD requires memory that scales with the full spatial grid, making large-scale 3D electromagnetic simulations prohibitively expensive; tensor-network compression offers a route to overcome this.
method: The field and auxiliary quantities are represented as comb tensor networks with local and global smoothing rank-reduction strategies, yielding CTN-FDTD updates with logarithmic memory and per-time-step cost.
result: CTN-FDTD simulates 35 trillion 3D grid points on a single node where standard FDTD would need 281 TB per array, and is demonstrated on a million-point 2D photonic crystal and an 8.6-billion-point 3D scattering problem.
conclusion: CTN representations substantially extend the reach of FDTD to extremely large electromagnetic problems, validated across varied sources, frequencies, and permittivity profiles.

title: Drinfeld Presentation Of Affine Iquantum Groups Via iHopf Algebras
authors: Xiaolong Pan Ming Lu
abstract: ArXiv:2610.30521v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Affine quantum groups [MATH] and affine iquantum groups [MATH] admit two complementary descriptions: a Serre-type presentation and a Drinfeld (current) presentation. While iquantum groups [MATH] are typically defined via the Serre presentation, their Drinfeld presentations are substantially more subtle and less well understood. In this paper, we give a conceptual derivation of the Drinfeld presentation of [MATH] starting directly from the Drinfeld presentation of [MATH], working within the framework of iHopf algebras. This approach leads naturally to the definition of iquantum affinization associated with arbitrary Kac-Moody algebras [MATH]. We further show that, in this general setting, these iquantum affinizations can be realized as coideal subalgebras of quantum affinizations with respect to the Drinfeld coproduct. Finally, in the affine case, we describe the imaginary root vectors [MATH] of [MATH] explicitly in terms of the root vectors [MATH] of [MATH], thereby extending the results of Li and Prze\'zdziecki for certain affine types of [MATH].
tldr: The paper gives a conceptual derivation of Drinfeld presentations for affine iquantum groups using iHopf algebras and coideal subalgebras.
motivation: Affine iquantum groups usually have Serre presentations, while their Drinfeld current presentations are more subtle and less understood.
method: The authors work in the framework of iHopf algebras, derive the Drinfeld presentation of affine iquantum groups from that of affine quantum groups, and define iquantum affinizations for arbitrary Kac-Moody algebras.
result: They show that these iquantum affinizations are coideal subalgebras of quantum affinizations with respect to the Drinfeld coproduct and explicitly describe imaginary root vectors in the affine case.
conclusion: The work extends algebraic results on Drinfeld presentations and root vectors for iquantum groups, but it is purely mathematical and not connected to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: The Reverse Ritz Inclusion: Computable Bounds On The Pseudospectra Of An Operator By Those Of A Finite-rank Compression
authors: Isaia Nisoli
abstract: ArXiv:2610.30530v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider a bounded operator on a separable complex Hilbert space, reached only through its action on vectors and that of its adjoint, and split it along a subspace of finite dimension into a compression, a far block acting on the complement, and the two couplings between them. Given upper bounds on the norms of the couplings and of the far block, we show that outside a disc a pseudospectrum of the operator lies in a pseudospectrum of the compression, with an explicit loss in the level; this reverses the classical inclusion of the Ritz values in a pseudospectrum of the operator. The same bounds, with the smallest singular value of the shifted compression, bound the resolvent of the operator, count its eigenvalues with algebraic multiplicity inside every contour outside the disc on which a computed inequality holds, and enclose its spectral projector; no normality, self-adjointness or positivity is used.
tldr: The paper proves reverse Ritz-inclusion bounds showing that pseudospectra of a bounded Hilbert-space operator can be controlled by pseudospectra of a finite-rank compression, with explicit resolvent and spectral-projector enclosures.
motivation: Classical Ritz-value theory gives inclusion of compressed eigenvalues in the operator pseudospectrum; the author seeks a converse direction that yields computable bounds on the full operator from finite-dimensional compression data.
method: The operator is decomposed along a finite-dimensional subspace into a compression, a far block, and coupling terms; assuming norm bounds on the couplings and far block, the author derives pseudospectral inclusion and resolvent bounds using the smallest singular value of the shifted compression.
result: Outside an explicit disc, the operator pseudospectrum is contained in a level-shifted pseudospectrum of the compression, and the same estimates count eigenvalues with algebraic multiplicity inside contours and enclose the spectral projector without normality or self-adjointness assumptions.
conclusion: The work provides a general computable finite-rank compression framework for rigorous spectral and pseudospectral enclosures of non-normal operators.

title: Not Where You Think: Protecting Location Privacy Against Reasoning-Based Geolocation
authors: Shanghao Shi, Jian Xiao, Hao Li, Yuanhaur Chang, Yevgeniy Vorobeychik, Nathan Jacobs, Neal Patwari, Ning Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2610.30439v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recent large reasoning models can infer where ordinary photos were taken using only visual information, creating a serious location privacy risk even when metadata and obvious geographic identifiers are removed. To understand the mechanism behind such fine-grained localization, we develop GeoTrace, a structured reasoning attack that exposes how models extract location-relevant visual clues and compose them through coarse-to-fine geographic reasoning. We evaluate GeoTrace on a worldwide benchmark of 525 ordinary images spanning natural, urban, residential, and human-centered scenes while excluding famous landmarks and direct location indicators. Our results show that GeoTrace localizes 25.71% of images within 1 km with Gemini-3-Flash and 16.95% with GPT-5-mini. More importantly, our analysis reveals a key insight in the visual clue chain: broad scene properties mainly support coarse localization, whereas precise localization disproportionately relies on small, distinctive, and editable local clues. Building on this insight, we develop GeoShift, a proactive user-side defense that breaks the visual clue chain before image release. Rather than simply removing geographic evidence, GeoShift preserves stable scene properties, selects a visually compatible false target location, and strategically rewrites high-impact geo-revealing clues to construct a coherent alternative geographic hypothesis. Experiments show that GeoShift reduces street-level localization from 16.95% to 2.48% under GPT-5-mini and from 25.71% to 3.81% under Gemini-3-Flash, while preserving visual quality and remaining effective against adaptive attacks.
tldr: The paper studies how large reasoning models infer photo locations from visual clues and proposes a user-side image-editing defense to disrupt this inference.
motivation: Reasoning-capable vision models can geolocate ordinary photos even without metadata or obvious landmarks, creating a serious privacy risk that needs mechanistic understanding and practical defenses.
method: The authors introduce GeoTrace, a structured coarse-to-fine reasoning attack, and GeoShift, a defense that preserves stable scene properties while rewriting high-impact local geo-revealing clues to create a coherent false location hypothesis.
result: GeoTrace localizes 25.71% of images within 1 km using Gemini-3-Flash and 16.95% using GPT-5-mini; GeoShift reduces street-level localization to 3.81% and 2.48%, respectively, while preserving visual quality.
conclusion: Location privacy against reasoning-based geolocation depends on disrupting small distinctive visual clues, and proactive clue-rewriting defenses can substantially reduce localization accuracy.

title: Reconfigurable Free-Space Optical Interconnects
authors: Jaekwon Lee, Carson G. Valdez, Anne R. Kroo, David A. B. Miller, Olav Solgaard
abstract: ArXiv:2610.30757v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Free-space optical interconnects can support many low-data-rate channels while avoiding the cost, energy consumption, and packaging constraints of optical waveguide- or fiber-based systems that are widely used today. We propose a free-space optical interconnect system based on reconfigurable micromirror arrays, and show that it scales favorably due to its two-dimensional scaling. We discuss the channel count scaling model, compare our demonstration with theory, and project a channel count above 10,000 to achieve 100 Tbps with slow channels (e.g., <10 Gbps). In a proof-of-concept system with a piston-motion micromirror array, we demonstrate nine channels that are simultaneously optimized. The optimization enables -21.7 dB of average worst-case crosstalk for a channel pitch equal to twice the beam radius, a smaller channel spacing than that required in flat tip-tilt mirrors. The optimization flow is further investigated for different channel spacings, simultaneous illumination, and different numbers of outputs, which generally achieve smaller worst-case crosstalk than the flat tip-tilt mirror case. Overall, the work demonstrates the advantage of piston-motion micromirrors in the proposed optical interconnects.
tldr: The paper proposes a reconfigurable free-space optical interconnect built on piston-motion micromirror arrays, showing favorable 2D channel-count scaling and demonstrating nine simultaneously optimized channels with -21.7 dB worst-case crosstalk.
motivation: Waveguide- and fiber-based optical links impose cost, energy, and packaging constraints, so the authors aim for a scalable free-space alternative that supports many low-data-rate channels.
method: They develop a channel-count scaling model, build a proof-of-concept system with a piston-motion micromirror array, and run an optimization flow for simultaneous multi-channel illumination, comparing against flat tip-tilt mirror configurations at various channel spacings.
result: The demonstration achieves nine simultaneously optimized channels with -21.7 dB average worst-case crosstalk at a channel pitch of twice the beam radius, and projections indicate over 10,000 slow channels could reach 100 Tbps aggregate throughput.
conclusion: Piston-motion micromirrors enable denser channel packing and lower crosstalk than flat tip-tilt mirrors, making reconfigurable free-space interconnects a viable scalable approach for high-channel-count optical data links.

title: Light Pulse Propagation Through A Dielectric Slab. Ii. Two Roads To The Same Field: Numerical Cross-validation Of Local (fdtd-ade) And Non-local (retarded Integral-equation) Solutions
authors: Giancarlo Reali
abstract: ArXiv:2610.30833v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Paper I of this series (arXiv:2610.29336) solves, via the retarded Green's functions, the local differential equations governing light propagation in a plane-parallel dielectric slab, obtaining a pair of retarded integral equations that represent, at the continuum level, the microscopic multiple-scattering picture underlying the local formulation. The two formulations are thus proven to be analytically equivalent. The local system of differential equations is then solved numerically with a finite-difference time-domain scheme (FDTD-ADE). This report closes the loop by solving the retarded integral equations directly, without passing through the local formulation, and comparing the result with the FDTD-ADE solution under the same physical and material conditions. The two independently implemented, structurally different numerical schemes agree within 0.02-1.3% for the reported reflected and transmitted energy fractions; the absorbed fraction, computed independently in both schemes from the Lorentz damping term rather than merely inferred from 1-R-T, agrees closely between the two methods, to the precision reported. Both solutions are also compared with an exact reference, the Airy formula weighted over the pulse spectrum: the direct solution reproduces it to within 0.3%, and its Richardson extrapolation to all digits shown. The agreement persists for a few-cycle pulse and for a sub-wavelength slab, where naive fixed-point iteration of the integral equations is not a practical convergent strategy. A complementary set of movie-style, nine-frame visualizations is also presented, illustrating the same equivalence directly in the field rather than only in integrated observables. To the author's knowledge, a direct numerical cross-validation of these two formulations in this genuinely time-dependent regime has not previously been reported.
tldr: The paper numerically cross-validates two classical electrodynamics formulations — FDTD-ADE solution of local differential equations and direct solution of retarded integral equations — for light pulse propagation through a plane-parallel dielectric slab.
motivation: Paper I established analytic equivalence between the local differential formulation and the non-local retarded integral-equation formulation; this work aims to confirm that equivalence at the numerical level in a genuinely time-dependent regime.
method: The retarded integral equations are solved directly, without recourse to the local formulation, and compared against an independent FDTD-ADE scheme for reflected, transmitted, and absorbed energy fractions under matched physical and material conditions, with the Airy formula weighted by the pulse spectrum used as an exact reference.
result: The two structurally distinct numerical schemes agree to within 0.02–1.3% for reflected and transmitted energy fractions, the absorbed fraction computed from the Lorentz damping term agrees closely, and the direct solution reproduces the spectrally weighted Airy reference to within 0.3%, including for few-cycle pulses and sub-wavelength slabs.
conclusion: The numerical cross-validation supports the analytic equivalence between the local and non-local descriptions and demonstrates that direct integral-equation solution is practical where fixed-point iteration fails; the work is purely classical optics with no quantum information or thermodynamic content.

title: When Language Models Misinterpret Uncertainty In Earth System Mechanism Attribution
authors: Nan Chen Pouria Behnoudfar
abstract: ArXiv:2610.30501v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Mechanistic attribution in Earth system science requires quantifying uncertainty and communicating its implications. Here, we develop an uncertainty-aware mechanistic attribution pipeline that constructs probabilistic fingerprints from ensemble estimates, including covariance-aware separation of competing mechanisms, and an evidence ladder that systematically varies the information provided to language models (LLMs). We evaluate this framework in an idealized stochastic system and a coupled El Ni\~no model using controlled interventions and ensemble data assimilation. In the idealized system, numerical separation increases GPT-4o's intervention-label agreement from 0.80 to 0.98, but not GPT-4o-mini's. In the coupled system, both LLMs identify seven of eight fingerprint-ambiguous events when given full fingerprints with verbal interpretations; GPT-4o's false ambiguity reports decrease from 10/82 to 1/82, without consistent gains in intervention-label agreement. For eight historical ENSO events, the uncertainty-aware condition agrees with the model-inferred mechanism labels in seven cases. These findings distinguish uncertainty assessment from its communication.
tldr: The paper develops an uncertainty-aware mechanistic attribution pipeline for Earth system science and evaluates how language models interpret probabilistic fingerprints in idealized and ENSO-like systems.
motivation: Mechanistic attribution in Earth system science requires robust uncertainty quantification and clear communication of uncertainty to decision-makers and AI systems.
method: The authors construct probabilistic fingerprints from ensemble estimates, perform covariance-aware separation of competing mechanisms, and use an evidence ladder that varies the information supplied to LLMs, testing the approach in an idealized stochastic system and a coupled El Niño model.
result: Numerical separation improves GPT-4o's intervention-label agreement in the idealized system, while full fingerprints with verbal interpretations help both LLMs identify most ambiguous events and reduce GPT-4o's false ambiguity reports in the coupled system.
conclusion: The findings show that assessing uncertainty and communicating it to LLMs are distinct challenges, with implications for mechanistic attribution in Earth system science.

title: On Borodin-Gorin Presentation Of Heckman-Opdam $\mathfrak{gl}_n$ Hypergeometric Function
authors: S. Khoroshkin L. Cherepanov
abstract: ArXiv:2610.30304v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that Borodin-Gorin presentation for Heckman-Opdam [MATH] hypergeometric function by interlacing integrals is equivalent to two other integral presentations studied in arXiv:2508.18864. We also consider related Baxter operators and the corresponding limiting procedure from the Ruijsenaars hyperbolic model.
tldr: The paper proves equivalence between Borodin-Gorin integral presentations of the Heckman-Opdam gl_n hypergeometric function and two other integral representations.
motivation: The authors aim to clarify the relationships among several integral presentations of Heckman-Opdam hypergeometric functions and connect them to Baxter operators and the Ruijsenaars hyperbolic model.
method: They establish equivalence of the Borodin-Gorin presentation by interlacing integrals with two previously studied integral presentations, and analyze related Baxter operators via a limiting procedure from the Ruijsenaars hyperbolic model.
result: The Borodin-Gorin presentation is shown to be equivalent to the other integral presentations, with the analysis yielding corresponding Baxter operator relations and limiting connections.
conclusion: The work unifies different integral representations of Heckman-Opdam hypergeometric functions and clarifies their relation to Baxter operators and integrable hyperbolic models.

title: Efficient Third-harmonic Generation In high-Q Tantalum Pentoxide Microcavities
authors: Xinke Xing, Yixuan Yang, Xinzhi Zheng, Renhong Gao, Li Deng, Jintian Lin, Ya Cheng
abstract: ArXiv:2610.30579v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Nonlinear harmonic generation in microcavities offers a compelling route toward energy efficient on-chip short-wavelength coherent light sources, enabled by tight optical confinement within compact mode volumes and flexible dispersion engineering. Tantalum pentoxide (Ta2O5) photonic platforms are particularly promising for realizing such nonlinear processes: their broad transparency window (280-8000 nm) supports broadband operation, their large bandgap suppresses two-photon absorption, and their thick-film deposition capability enables dispersion management--features that can collectively enhance the performance of nonlinear light sources. Here, we demonstrate, to the best of our knowledge, the first efficient third-harmonic generation (THG) in high-Q Ta2O5 microcavities. These microcavities feature smooth surfaces and high loaded Q factors up to 2.67X10^6, thereby facilitating nonlinear interactions. Through dispersion engineering, efficient THG is realized in both suspended microdisks and monolithic microrings under telecom-band continuous-wave laser pumping, as confirmed by optical spectra, visible-light microscopy, and the near-cubic pump-power dependence of the conversion efficiency. This work lays a foundation for chip-scale f-3f self-referencing of frequency combs and next-generation integrated nonlinear photonics.
tldr: Demonstrates efficient third-harmonic generation in high-Q tantalum pentoxide microdisk and microring microcavities under telecom-band continuous-wave pumping.
motivation: On-chip short-wavelength coherent light sources require strong optical confinement, broad transparency, and dispersion engineering; Ta2O5 offers these advantages but efficient THG had not yet been shown in high-Q Ta2O5 cavities.
method: Fabricated smooth suspended microdisks and monolithic microrings with loaded Q factors up to 2.67x10^6, engineered dispersion, and pumped with telecom continuous-wave lasers while characterizing the harmonic via optical spectra and visible-light microscopy.
result: Efficient THG was observed in both cavity geometries, confirmed by the near-cubic pump-power dependence of conversion efficiency, indicating a third-order nonlinear process.
conclusion: Establishes Ta2O5 microcavity platforms as a foundation for chip-scale f-3f self-referencing of frequency combs and integrated nonlinear photonics.

title: Alignment-Free Optical Combining With Scalar-Message Expectation Propagation Detection For Distributed Multi-Aperture Coherent Reception
authors: Mingwen Zhu, Yiqun Zhang, Liyu Sun, Ming Liu, Changwei Wang, Jiayin Xue
abstract: ArXiv:2610.30600v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose an alignment-free distributed multi-aperture optical receiver with a single coherent front end, in which the differential delays between apertures are large. The branch signals are optically combined without inter-branch delay or phase alignment. Large differential delays produce separated tap clusters, forming a sparse ISI channel with long memory. Scalar-message expectation propagation exploits this sparsity to recover the transmitted symbols. Simulations show lower BER than equal-area single-aperture reception and no clear BER degradation over the tested delay spans. As the maximum differential delay increases from 100.5 to 200.5 symbol periods, the channel span nearly doubles, while the factor-graph edge count increases by only about 1.5\%. The trade-off is higher BER than ideal coherent combining schemes in exchange for fewer coherent front ends than digital combining and no inter-branch delay or phase alignment before optical combining.
tldr: The paper proposes an alignment-free distributed multi-aperture coherent optical receiver that optically combines branch signals without delay or phase alignment, using scalar-message expectation propagation detection to exploit the resulting sparse long-memory ISI channel.
motivation: Distributed multi-aperture reception with a single coherent front end could reduce hardware cost, but large differential delays between apertures make conventional alignment and digital combining impractical.
method: Branch signals with large differential delays are optically combined without alignment, producing separated tap clusters that form a sparse ISI channel with long memory; a scalar-message expectation propagation detector on the factor graph then recovers the transmitted symbols.
result: Simulations show lower BER than equal-area single-aperture reception with no clear degradation across tested delay spans; as the maximum differential delay grows from 100.5 to 200.5 symbol periods, the channel span nearly doubles while factor-graph edge count grows only ~1.5%.
conclusion: The scheme trades some BER performance relative to ideal coherent combining for fewer coherent front ends and elimination of inter-branch delay/phase alignment before optical combining.

title: Laser-design Methodology For Extending An Available Wavelength Range Of Dual-wavelength Injection-seeded Laser
authors: Ayaka Hashimoto, Tetsuto Watanabe. Sota Kobayashi, Megumi Otose, Ken'ichi Nakagawa, Masayuki Katsuragawa
abstract: ArXiv:2610.30897v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper describes a method for expanding the applicable wavelength range of dual-wavelength oscillation injection-locked lasers. Special focus is placed on the laser design that enables simultaneous oscillations at both the gain center and gain tail, requiring the most stringent requirements. We show that a sufficient performance can be achieved by introducing a wavelength-dependence property onto the output coupling mirror, without giving any losses in the laser resonator. We also show how we can determine such wavelength-dependent property on the basis of experimental measurements. Using the designed output-coupler, in practices, we demonstrate simultaneous oscillations with an equal output power, across a variety of wavelength combinations of near the gain center and around the gain tail in which the wavelength separation amounts 60 nm at the most.
tldr: The paper presents a laser-design methodology that extends the usable wavelength range of dual-wavelength injection-seeded lasers by engineering the wavelength-dependent properties of the output coupling mirror.
motivation: Dual-wavelength oscillation injection-locked lasers are limited in the wavelength separations they can support, especially when simultaneous oscillation at both the gain center and gain tail is required under stringent conditions.
method: The authors introduce wavelength-dependent reflectivity into the output coupler to balance gain differences without adding intra-cavity loss, and they determine the required coupler properties from experimental measurements.
result: Using the designed output coupler, they demonstrate simultaneous dual-wavelength oscillation with equal output power across wavelength combinations spanning up to 60 nm separation.
conclusion: Wavelength-dependent output coupling provides a practical route to broaden the applicable wavelength range of dual-wavelength injection-seeded lasers without compromising resonator performance.

title: A Smooth Riemannian Metric On An Arbitrary Product Of Spheres With Bernoulli Geodesic Flow
authors: Keith Burns, Tomas Gedeon, Yuping Ruan
abstract: ArXiv:2610.30464v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct a smooth Riemannian metric on an arbitrary product of spheres whose geodesic flow is Bernoulli with respect to the Liouville measure.
tldr: The authors construct a smooth Riemannian metric on an arbitrary product of spheres whose geodesic flow is Bernoulli with respect to the Liouville measure.
motivation: Bernoulli property is the strongest form of stochastic behavior for dynamical systems, and it is known that such behavior can be achieved by suitable geometric deformations; products of spheres are a natural testbed for these constructions.
method: A geometric construction of a smooth Riemannian metric on a product of spheres is designed and analyzed to show that its geodesic flow, with respect to Liouville measure, is measurably isomorphic to a Bernoulli shift.
result: The paper establishes the existence of such a metric for any number of spherical factors, yielding Bernoulli geodesic flow.
conclusion: The work extends results on stochastic geodesic flows to arbitrary products of spheres, purely within ergodic theory and differential geometry.

title: Discovery Of Singularities In Partial Differential Equations Using Adaptive Numerical Discretizations
authors: Allen Yang, Lucas Amoudruz, Petros Koumoutsakos
abstract: ArXiv:2610.30492v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We compute self-similar singularity profiles of partial differential equations (PDEs) using adaptive numerical discretizations based on optimizing a discrete loss (ODIL). The fields are represented in overlapping local Chebyshev patches joined with a mapped asymptotic patch. After factoring out the leading power laws of solution ansatzes, their limiting amplitudes at infinity are determined by the optimization, eliminating domain truncation and prescribed far-field conditions. Adaptive refinement is guided by Chebyshev-coefficient decay, and the nonlinear least-squares problem is solved using automatically differentiated Gauss--Newton iterations with Levenberg--Marquardt damping. The method achieves O(10^{-14})-level accuracy for Burgers profiles, residuals of O(10^{-14}) to O(10^{-10}) for the generalized De Gregorio family, and of O(10^{-8}) in a local region for the two-dimensional Boussinesq equations. These results demonstrate that ODIL can identify singularity profiles for PDEs with high accuracy using adaptive numerical methods, complementing ongoing efforts that rely on artificial intelligence.
tldr: The paper presents ODIL, an adaptive Chebyshev-patch numerical method for computing self-similar singularity profiles of nonlinear PDEs such as Burgers, De Gregorio, and 2D Boussinesq equations.
motivation: Singularity formation in PDEs is hard to resolve numerically because solutions blow up and require domain truncation and prescribed far-field conditions; the authors aim to remove these artefacts.
method: Fields are represented in overlapping local Chebyshev patches joined to a mapped asymptotic patch, with leading power laws factored out; amplitudes at infinity are determined by a nonlinear least-squares optimization solved with automatically differentiated Gauss-Newton/Levenberg-Marquardt iterations, refined via Chebyshev-coefficient decay.
result: The method reaches O(1e-14) accuracy for Burgers profiles, residuals of O(1e-14)-O(1e-10) for the generalized De Gregorio family, and O(1e-8) locally for 2D Boussinesq equations.
conclusion: Adaptive discrete-loss optimization (ODIL) can accurately identify PDE singularity profiles, complementing AI-based approaches.

title: High-Order Fully Discrete Entropy-Stable Dg Methods With Compact Explicit Single-Step Time Discretizations
authors: Yuchang Liu, Yan Jiang, Mengping Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2610.30535v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a unified framework for high-order, fully discrete entropy-stable discontinuous Galerkin (DG) methods with compact explicit single-step time discretizations. At the end of each time step, the preliminary DG polynomial is scaled toward its cell average to enforce a strong cell entropy inequality while preserving conservation. This correction is feasible if and only if the updated cell average satisfies a weak cell entropy inequality, which standard third-order strong-stability-preserving Runge--Kutta DG updates can violate at arbitrarily small positive CFL numbers. For compact single-step schemes, including compact Runge--Kutta, Lax--Wendroff, and ADER-DG methods, we derive an explicit interval of feasible numerical entropy fluxes at each interface and prove that it is nonempty under a CFL condition. Projecting a compatible high-order target flux onto this interval guarantees the weak cell entropy inequality and preserves single-step high-order accuracy on smooth solutions, including near nondegenerate extrema. The limiter also enforces multiple entropy inequalities simultaneously. We also establish a Lax--Wendroff-type theorem. Numerical experiments for scalar conservation laws and the compressible Euler equations demonstrate high-order accuracy, multi-entropy control, and robustness for strong shocks.
tldr: The paper develops entropy-stable fully discrete discontinuous Galerkin methods with compact explicit single-step time discretizations for conservation laws.
motivation: Standard high-order DG time-stepping can violate cell entropy inequalities at small CFL numbers, so the authors seek robust entropy-stable compact schemes.
method: They introduce a cell-average-preserving scaling limiter and derive feasible intervals for numerical entropy fluxes, proving nonemptiness under a CFL condition for compact RK, Lax-Wendroff, and ADER-DG schemes.
result: The framework preserves high-order accuracy on smooth solutions, enforces multiple entropy inequalities, and satisfies a Lax-Wendroff-type theorem, with numerical tests for scalar laws and Euler equations.
conclusion: The proposed methods provide a unified route to high-order entropy-stable DG discretizations with compact explicit time stepping and strong-shock robustness.

title: Detecting Ai Training In Datacentre Power
authors: Tom Kimpson, Mauricio Baker, Emlyn Graham
abstract: ArXiv:2610.30182v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: AI governance agreements require methods to detect large model training runs on a monitored computing cluster, without trusting the operator. We develop a method to detect synchronous model training in facility-level power by Viterbi tracking of the wandering iteration cadence.
