On simulated datacentre power, when the operator makes no attempt to hide, the Viterbi tracker detects at least [MATH] of training runs against a declared inference workload, at a [MATH] false-alarm rate and within [MATH] of the Neyman--Pearson optimum, given a meter that samples at [MATH] Hz or faster. Of eight adversarial strategies an operator might use to hide, only extreme variation of the work per iteration evades the tracker. Its strongest form hides training in up to [MATH] of five-minute observations, but over a day at least [MATH] of such runs are still caught, at a [MATH] false-alarm rate per run. This adversarial strategy costs no throughput, but in small-scale training the operator needs [MATH]--[MATH] more compute to reach the same loss. A modest passive meter is sufficient to make hidden training both detectable and expensive, which makes power metering a promising part of compute verification that does not depend on trusting the operator.
tldr: The paper develops a Viterbi-based detector that identifies synchronous AI model training from facility-level power measurements, enabling untrusted-operator verification of compute usage.
motivation: AI governance agreements need ways to verify whether large training runs occurred on a monitored cluster without relying on the operator's self-reporting.
method: The authors model the wandering iteration cadence of training workloads and apply Viterbi tracking to simulated datacentre power traces, benchmarking against the Neyman-Pearson optimum and testing eight adversarial concealment strategies.
result: The tracker detects nearly all non-adversarial training runs at a 1% false-alarm rate close to the optimal bound; only extreme per-iteration work variation reliably evades it, and that strategy imposes large compute overhead for small-scale training.
conclusion: A modest passive power meter can make hidden AI training both detectable and costly, positioning power metering as a promising trustless component of compute verification.

title: Membership Inference Attack On Private Evolution
authors: Daniil Filienko, Sikha Pentyala, Martine de Cock
abstract: ArXiv:2610.30514v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Synthetic Data Generation (SDG) is an actively studied way to enable safe sharing of private data more broadly. Inference-only SDG methods, such as Private Evolution (PE), are particularly appealing, as they can leverage black-box access to pre-trained foundation models to generate high quality data without the need for model fine-tuning on the private data. PE is explicitly designed to produce synthetic data under Differential Privacy (DP). Yet formal DP guarantees do not eliminate the need for empirical privacy auditing of the practical susceptibility of released synthetic data to adversarial attacks. In this work, we introduce the first white-box Membership Inference Attack (MIA) tailored to the voting-based algorithm underlying the PE framework. By exploiting how the iterative filtering process biases the survival and proximity of synthetic candidates toward private instances, our attack achieves empirical performance indicating private data leakage in the PE applications across image, text, and tabular modalities.
tldr: The paper introduces the first white-box membership inference attack against the voting-based algorithm of Private Evolution (PE), an inference-only differentially private synthetic data generation framework, showing empirical privacy leakage across image, text, and tabular modalities.
motivation: Differential privacy guarantees do not preclude practical leakage in released synthetic data, so empirical privacy auditing of inference-only SDG methods like PE is needed.
method: The authors design a white-box MIA that exploits how PE's iterative filtering biases the survival and proximity of synthetic candidates toward private instances, and evaluate it on image, text, and tabular data.
result: The attack achieves empirical performance indicating private data leakage in PE applications across all three modalities, despite the DP design.
conclusion: Formal DP bounds alone are insufficient; empirical auditing of PE-style synthetic data pipelines is necessary to assess real-world privacy risk.

title: A Weakly Group Strategy-Proof And Pareto-Stable Matching Mechanism With Two-Sided Indifferences Under Gross Substitutes
authors: Ryosuke Sato Yasushi Kawase
abstract: ArXiv:2610.30807v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study finite many-to-one matching markets with indifferences on both sides and publicly known firm preferences over sets of workers. A standard approach breaks ties uniformly at random and runs deferred acceptance, which is strategy-proof for workers but may select a weakly stable matching that is Pareto dominated under the agents' original preferences. For the broad class of markets in which each firm's preferences admit a gross substitutes (GS) representation, we construct a deterministic generalized deferred acceptance mechanism that is weakly stable, Pareto efficient with respect to both sides, worker weakly group strategy-proof, and implementable in strongly polynomial time given value oracles for the GS representations. This domain includes nonresponsive firm preferences, such as additive scores under matroid constraints and assignment values. Our analysis bridges ordinal matching with indifferences and competitive equilibria under imperfectly transferable utility. Although the mechanism uses only ordinal comparisons, it returns a seller-optimal equilibrium matching of a tiered auxiliary market, and the equilibrium structure of this market yields the stability, efficiency, and incentive guarantees.
tldr: The paper designs a deterministic generalized deferred-acceptance mechanism for many-to-one matching markets with indifferences on both sides and gross-substitutes firm preferences, achieving weak stability, two-sided Pareto efficiency, and weak group strategy-proofness for workers in strongly polynomial time.
motivation: Random tie-breaking plus deferred acceptance is strategy-proof for workers but can yield weakly stable matchings that are Pareto dominated under the agents' original preferences, so a deterministic mechanism with stronger efficiency and incentive guarantees is needed.
method: For markets where firm preferences admit a gross substitutes representation, the authors construct a generalized deferred acceptance mechanism using only ordinal comparisons, and they relate its outcome to a seller-optimal equilibrium of a tiered auxiliary market with imperfectly transferable utility.
result: The mechanism is weakly stable, Pareto efficient for both sides, worker weakly group strategy-proof, and implementable in strongly polynomial time given value oracles, covering nonresponsive preferences such as additive scores under matroid constraints and assignment values.
conclusion: The work bridges ordinal matching with indifferences and competitive equilibrium analysis, showing that equilibrium structure in a tiered auxiliary market can deliver stability, efficiency, and incentive guarantees simultaneously.

title: Weaponizing The Exit: Input Privacy Leakage Via Exit Routing Manipulation In Multi-Exit Networks
authors: Yulong Tian, Lei Wang, Jincan Yang, Hao Wu, Hao Han, Fengyuan Xu, Sheng Zhong
abstract: ArXiv:2610.31246v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Multi-exit networks improve inference efficiency by allowing inputs to terminate early at intermediate exits. We identify a privacy vulnerability in cloud deployments of these networks: a malicious Cloud Service Provider (CSP) can infer sensitive properties of individual user inputs solely from inference latency, without accessing inputs, intermediate states, or model outputs. The attack exploits the CSP's control over the model supply chain. Prior to deployment, the CSP supplies a specially crafted multi-exit network manipulated so that inputs carrying a target sensitive property are routed to a designated exit with high probability, while other inputs exit elsewhere. At serving time, the CSP infers the exit index from per-query latency, thereby determining whether each input possesses the target property without accessing inputs, outputs, or internal model states. We propose a training framework combining selective label smoothing and entropy-covariance optimization to control confidence distributions across exits and reduce premature termination. We conduct experiments on four datasets across ten target properties. The results demonstrate strong attack effectiveness and stealthiness. The attack achieves an average F1 score of 0.73, compared to 0.25 for the strongest baseline, while main task accuracy drops by less than 1.3\% and inference speedup degradation remains below 0.1 in most settings. Our code is available at [URL].
tldr: A malicious cloud provider can infer sensitive properties of user inputs in multi-exit neural networks by weaponizing exit routing so that per-query inference latency reveals the exit index, and hence the property, without accessing inputs, outputs, or internal states.
motivation: Multi-exit networks are deployed in the cloud for efficiency, giving the model supplier control over the supply chain; the authors ask whether that control can be converted into a privacy side channel based purely on latency.
method: The provider ships a crafted multi-exit model trained with selective label smoothing plus entropy-covariance optimization to steer inputs with a target property toward a designated exit while suppressing premature termination; at serving time the exit index is inferred from per-query latency.
result: Across four datasets and ten target properties the attack reaches an average F1 of 0.73 versus 0.25 for the strongest baseline, with main-task accuracy dropping under 1.3% and speedup degradation below 0.1 in most settings.
conclusion: Exit routing in multi-exit networks constitutes a practical latency-based privacy leak that is effective and stealthy, highlighting supply-chain risks in cloud inference.

title: Spin-Clifford Bundles And Spin Connections On The Hyperbolic Clifford Algebra - Part I
authors: J. M. Hoff Da Silva E. Notte-Cuello
abstract: ArXiv:2610.30542v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop the theory of spinor fields associated with the hyperbolic Clifford algebra [MATH], which is associated with hyperbolic space [MATH]. Algebraically, we exhibit an explicit real primitive idempotent which, unlike the Lorentzian case, remains primitive after complexification and generates the ideal of Witten superfields. We also describe the chirality decomposition and the hyperbolic spin group. Geometrically, we construct a canonical hyperbolic spin structure on every oriented manifold, showing that no topological obstructions arise beyond orientability and we study the associated spinor bundles, spin-Clifford bundles and ideal spinor subbundles. Finally, we introduce the isotropic extension of an arbitrary linear connection to [MATH], which is always compatible with the hyperbolic metric, and the associated hyperbolic spin connection, whose well-definedness, compatibilities, curvature and explicit form are established, providing the geometric framework for Dirac operators on the hyperbolic Clifford algebra, which we will present in a forthcoming article.
tldr: The paper develops spinor fields, spin-Clifford bundles, and spin connections associated with the hyperbolic Clifford algebra on hyperbolic space.
motivation: The authors aim to extend spinor and Clifford bundle constructions from the Lorentzian setting to the hyperbolic Clifford algebra and hyperbolic space.
method: They construct a real primitive idempotent, describe chirality and the hyperbolic spin group, build canonical hyperbolic spin structures, and introduce isotropic extensions of linear connections and hyperbolic spin connections.
result: The paper shows that no topological obstruction arises beyond orientability, constructs associated spinor bundles and ideal subbundles, and establishes the well-definedness, compatibility, curvature, and explicit form of the hyperbolic spin connection.
conclusion: This provides a geometric framework for Dirac operators on the hyperbolic Clifford algebra, to be treated in a forthcoming article.

title: Core-periphery Structure Induces Double Phase Transitions In Information Cascades
authors: Jiaqi Nie, Xincheng Shu, Yong Min, Qi Xuan, Zhongyuan Ruan
abstract: ArXiv:2610.30745v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Double phase transitions in spreading processes are commonly associated with additional dynamical or structural complexity. Here, we show that such transitions can emerge naturally in prevalent networks exhibiting a core-periphery (CP) organization. Specifically, we consider threshold-driven spreading on CP networks constructed from the stochastic block model, which is characterized by three parameters: the relative core size [MATH], the CP coupling strength [MATH], and the fraction of intra-block link allocation [MATH]. We find that, by varying the allocation of links between the core and periphery, the system can generate a global cascade window in the parameter spaces, bounded by distinct phase transitions. At the upper boundary, where the periphery becomes sparse, the interplay between the structural inertia (resistance to state changes) of the core and the spreading constraints of the periphery can produce a double phase transition via a two-stage cascading mechanism. This double transition may change type from discontinuous-continuous to discontinuous-discontinuous as the model parameters vary in the limit of a vanishingly small initial seed. Our results reveal a simple structural route to double phase transitions of distinct types and highlight the role of CP structure in shaping threshold-driven spreading dynamics.
tldr: Threshold-driven spreading on core-periphery stochastic block model networks produces a cascade window bounded by two phase transitions, the upper one of which can become a double transition of mixed discontinuous/continuous or doubly discontinuous type.
motivation: Double phase transitions in spreading dynamics are usually attributed to added dynamical or structural complexity; the authors ask whether they can arise naturally from a common core-periphery network organization.
method: They construct core-periphery networks from a stochastic block model parameterized by relative core size, core-periphery coupling strength, and intra-block link allocation fraction, then analyze threshold-driven cascade dynamics as a function of these parameters and the initial seed size.
result: A global cascade window appears in parameter space, and near the upper boundary the interplay between core structural inertia and periphery sparsity yields a two-stage cascading mechanism producing a double transition whose type changes with model parameters in the vanishing-seed limit.
conclusion: Core-periphery organization offers a simple structural route to double phase transitions of distinct types, underscoring the role of mesoscale network structure in shaping threshold-driven spreading.

title: Consensus-Aware Co-design Of Wireless Multi-Agent Control And Communication Systems
authors: Atefeh Termehchi, Sajedeh Soleimani, Shiva Kazemi Taskooh, Mehdi Rasti, Ekram Hossain
abstract: ArXiv:2610.30141v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Autonomous multi-agent control systems (MACSs) enable distributed coordination in emerging applications such as smart power grids and autonomous vehicle or drone networks. In many of these applications, inter-agent communication relies on wireless networks. However, conventional MACS designs neglect the interaction between the communication and control subsystems. At the same time, conventional wireless designs reserve communication resources based on worst-case MACS requirements. Consequently, control performance is degraded and wireless resources are utilized inefficiently. To address these challenges, we propose a consensus-aware co-design approach for MACSs and wireless communication systems. We introduce a system model in which agents achieve consensus by exchanging information through device-to-device (D2D) links that share spectrum with cellular users under limited bandwidth resources. Based on this model, we formulate a joint optimization problem for consensus-topology selection and wireless resource allocation to minimize bandwidth consumption while guaranteeing consensus and satisfying the quality-of-service (QoS) requirements of both MACSs and cellular users. Although the resulting problem is a mixed-integer nonlinear program (NP-hard in general), a structural property of the optimal solution enables a sequential two-stage optimization algorithm with polynomial complexity. Simulations on a smart power grid case study demonstrate that the proposed approach achieves 24-27% bandwidth savings compared with the two baselines while maintaining consensus and satisfying all QoS requirements of the control agents and the communication users.
tldr: The paper proposes a consensus-aware co-design of wireless multi-agent control systems and D2D-based communication, jointly optimizing consensus topology selection and spectrum resource allocation to cut bandwidth use while preserving control consensus and QoS.
motivation: Conventional multi-agent control designs ignore the coupling between control and communication, while wireless designs over-provision resources for worst-case control needs, degrading control performance and wasting spectrum.
method: The authors build a model where agents reach consensus over D2D links sharing spectrum with cellular users, formulate a mixed-integer nonlinear joint optimization (NP-hard), and exploit structural properties to derive a polynomial-complexity two-stage sequential algorithm.
result: Simulations on a smart power grid case study show 24-27% bandwidth savings over two baselines while maintaining consensus and satisfying all control-agent and cellular-user QoS requirements.
conclusion: Co-designing consensus control with wireless resource allocation yields substantial spectral efficiency gains, though the work is classical networked control and communications with no quantum information or thermodynamic content.

title: Sufficient Conditions For Exact Convergence Time In Prescribed-Time Control
authors: Jiyuan Kuang
abstract: ArXiv:2610.30147v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we propose a series of theoretical results for prescribed-time control to rigorously prove that the closed-loop system will not reach the equilibrium point before the prescribed time. Thus, it is convenient to prove that the settling time is exactly equal to the prescribed time instant. In other words, conservative estimation of the settling time, which often accompanies classical finite-/fixed-time or prescribed-time control results, is theoretically avoided in this paper. Specifically, we introduce a local Lipschitz condition, a local homogeneous linear-growth condition, and an Osgood condition in sequence. Both reduction to absurdity and the Lyapunov method are applied to demonstrate that the system cannot converge to zero before the prescribed time instant. Finally, the proposed framework is applied to prescribed-time controllers based on adaptive backstepping, parametric Lyapunov equations, and distributed leader-following consensus, demonstrating the generality of the proposed results.
tldr: The paper derives sufficient conditions guaranteeing that prescribed-time controllers achieve convergence exactly at the prescribed time instant, with no early convergence and no conservative settling-time overestimation.
motivation: Classical finite-time, fixed-time, and prescribed-time control designs typically only guarantee an upper bound on settling time, so the actual convergence may occur earlier than intended; the author aims to eliminate this gap rigorously.
method: A local Lipschitz condition, a local homogeneous linear-growth condition, and an Osgood condition are introduced in sequence and combined with proof by contradiction and Lyapunov arguments to show the state cannot reach the origin before the prescribed time.
result: The framework is shown to apply to prescribed-time controllers built from adaptive backstepping, parametric Lyapunov equations, and distributed leader-following consensus, demonstrating that exact settling-time equality can be proven in each case.
conclusion: The proposed conditions provide a general and reusable toolkit for certifying exact prescribed-time convergence, avoiding the conservative settling-time estimates common in existing control designs.

title: Higher-order Tangent And Secant Numbers, Special-value Integrals, And A Common Zero Attractor
authors: Luc Rams\`es Talla Waffo
abstract: ArXiv:2610.30208v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study two families of coefficients associated with powers of the tangent function and with products of the secant and tangent functions, and develop a unified treatment of the corresponding higher-order tangent and secant numbers. The first part establishes a common identity for even derivatives of [MATH] and odd derivatives of [MATH]. Combined with integral formulae for these derivatives, this yields finite power-integral representations for the normalized values [MATH] and [MATH] and naturally introduces two polynomial families [MATH] and [MATH]. We determine several arithmetic and structural properties of these polynomials. In particular, we identify the exact content of [MATH], prove that [MATH] is primitive, establish strict log-concavity and unimodality of their coefficient sequences, and describe their real zeros. For even indices each family has a unique negative real zero, and the two sequences of real zeros have the same limit. We also derive differential recurrences and generating functions for [MATH] and [MATH]. The generating functions lead to a global complex-singularity analysis. We construct a compact Jordan curve [MATH] and prove that the complex zero sets of both [MATH] and [MATH] converge to [MATH] in Hausdorff distance. The normalized zero-counting measures converge weakly to the same equilibrium measure on [MATH]. We determine the logarithmic capacity of the enclosed compact set, give an explicit arclength density for the limiting measure, and compute its first moments. Numerical plots for [MATH], [MATH], [MATH] and [MATH] illustrate the zero-attractor theorem.
tldr: A pure-mathematics study of higher-order tangent and secant numbers, their associated polynomial families, and the common complex zero attractor of those polynomials.
motivation: The authors aim to unify the treatment of coefficients arising from powers of tangent and from secant–tangent products, and to characterize the arithmetic and analytic structure of the resulting normalized quantities and polynomials.
method: They establish identities for even derivatives of tan and odd derivatives of sec, combine them with integral formulae to obtain finite power-integral representations, and introduce two polynomial families whose content, primitivity, log-concavity, unimodality and real zeros are analyzed; generating functions then enable a complex-singularity analysis via a Jordan curve and potential-theoretic tools.
result: The polynomials are shown to have prescribed content, primitivity, strictly log-concave and unimodal coefficient sequences, and a unique negative real zero for even indices with a common limit; the complex zero sets converge in Hausdorff distance to a compact set whose equilibrium measure, logarithmic capacity, arclength density and first moments are computed explicitly.
conclusion: The work gives a coherent analytic and arithmetic account of higher-order tangent and secant numbers and proves a zero-attractor theorem for the associated polynomials, illustrated numerically.

title: Finite Zero Products Of Toeplitz Operators With Harmonic Symbols
authors: Youqi Liu, Jie Qin, Sui Huang
abstract: ArXiv:2610.30209v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study finite products of Toeplitz operators with harmonic symbols on the Fock space over the complex plane. If every symbol has the form [MATH], where [MATH] and [MATH] are entire functions of exponential type, we prove that a finite product vanishes if and only if one symbol vanishes identically. It suffices to test the product on reproducing kernels. The proof represents the product by a two-variable entire function and transforms the equation for a left factor by [MATH]. A Fock norm identity then permits cancellation of each nonzero factor.
tldr: The paper proves that a finite product of Toeplitz operators with harmonic symbols of exponential type on the Fock space vanishes only if one factor vanishes identically.
motivation: Zero-product problems for Toeplitz operators are central in operator theory on Bergman and Fock spaces, but finite products with harmonic symbols remain poorly understood.
method: The product is represented by a two-variable entire function, the equation for a left factor is transformed, and a Fock norm identity is used to cancel each nonzero factor; testing on reproducing kernels suffices.
result: A finite product vanishes identically if and only if at least one of the symbols is identically zero, for symbols of the stated exponential-type form.
conclusion: The result extends zero-product characterizations to finite products of Fock-space Toeplitz operators with harmonic symbols, with a technique based on reproducing kernels and norm identities.

title: A Transformer-based Approach For Real-time Multi-agent Path Planning With Varying Initial/Final Conditions
authors: Qian Zhang, Shanqing Liu, Jerome Darbon, George Karniadakis
abstract: ArXiv:2610.30388v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We address the problem of real-time multi-agent path planning under prescribed initial and final configurations, formulated as a high-dimensional optimal control problem subject to inter-agent collision avoidance and obstacle constraints. Classical solvers based on the Hamilton--Jacobi--Bellman equation or Pontryagin's maximum principle (PMP) become computationally intractable as the number of agents grows, due to the curse of dimensionality and the non-convexity introduced by interaction constraints. We propose OCFormer, a transformer-based neural network that parameterizes the inverse of a coordinate transformation mapping a simple, analytically tractable latent space, in which agents evolve independently under a decoupled Hamiltonian, to the physical space of the coupled, interacting system. The model is trained by minimizing a physics-informed loss comprising the Hamiltonian ODE residual from the PMP and a boundary matching term, without requiring pre-computed trajectory data. The self-attention mechanism endows OCFormer with permutation equivariance over agents, a structural symmetry that prior symplectic network approaches do not natively enforce. When trained on a distribution of boundary conditions, the amortized OCFormer produces near-optimal trajectories for unseen initial and final configurations in a single forward pass ([MATH]220ms), enabling real-time inference without retraining. We further introduce a lightweight transfer learning framework that adapts a pretrained OCFormer to out-of-distribution perturbations in seconds via L-BFGS fine-tuning. Numerical experiments on two- and three-dimensional multi-agent navigation with up to 128 agents demonstrate the scalability and efficiency of the proposed approach.
tldr: OCFormer, a transformer-based physics-informed neural network, amortizes high-dimensional multi-agent optimal control to produce near-optimal collision-free trajectories in a single forward pass (~220 ms).
motivation: Classical HJB- or PMP-based solvers for multi-agent path planning suffer from the curse of dimensionality and non-convex interaction constraints, making real-time planning intractable as agent number grows.
method: The authors learn the inverse of a coordinate transformation mapping a decoupled latent Hamiltonian system to the coupled physical system, training with a physics-informed loss (PMP Hamiltonian ODE residual plus boundary matching) and exploiting self-attention for permutation equivariance; a cheap L-BFGS transfer-learning step handles out-of-distribution boundary conditions.
result: Experiments in two and three dimensions with up to 128 agents show scalable, fast, near-optimal trajectory generation for unseen initial/final configurations without retraining.
conclusion: Transformer architectures with physics-informed losses offer a practical real-time alternative to classical optimal-control solvers for multi-agent navigation, with rapid adaptation to perturbed conditions.

title: Outage Analysis And Bilevel Resource Optimization In RIS-Assisted Clustered Uav-noma Networks
authors: Masoud Ghazikor, Ly V. Nguyen, Morteza Hashemi
abstract: ArXiv:2610.30410v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper investigates RIS-assisted downlink UAV communications based on NOMA. Since conventional NOMA becomes difficult to scale as the number of UAVs grows, we develop a cluster-based UAV-NOMA framework in which a BS serves multiple UAV groups with the aid of partitionable RISs. Within this framework, we consider direct, RIS-only indirect, and composite links, and develop an analytical model for the received SNR and outage performance under Nakagami-[MATH] and double Nakagami-[MATH] fading with imperfect SIC. To enable scalable transmission, we introduce a greedy RIS-aware (GRIS) clustering method, which groups UAVs according to spatial and channel-related features. Based on the resulting clusters and RIS assignment, we formulate an efficiency-reliability bilevel optimization problem that jointly optimizes inter-cluster BS power allocation, intra-cluster NOMA power coefficients, and RIS element assignment. Specifically, the outer efficiency problem maximizes the average throughput across clusters, while the inner reliability problem minimizes the worst-UAV outage probability within each cluster. To solve the formulated problem, we propose a two-level iterative framework consisting of an inter-cluster outer-efficiency solver (IOS) and an intra-cluster inner-reliability solver (I2S), where I2S combines a grid-based progressive search (GPS) for NOMA power refinement with reliability-guided RIS element reassignment, and IOS updates the BS power weights. Numerical results demonstrate the effectiveness of GRIS clustering, while pre-optimization analysis reveals efficiency-reliability trade-offs in power allocation. Baseline comparisons illustrate the ability of IOS-I2S to balance efficiency and reliability, while ablation studies highlight the importance of joint optimization.
tldr: This paper develops a cluster-based RIS-assisted UAV-NOMA downlink framework with analytical outage models and a bilevel optimization scheme for power allocation and RIS element assignment.
motivation: Conventional NOMA does not scale well as the number of UAVs grows, so the authors propose clustering UAVs into groups served with the aid of partitionable RISs to enable scalable, reliable transmission.
method: The authors derive received-SNR and outage-probability expressions under Nakagami-m and double Nakagami-m fading with imperfect SIC, introduce a greedy RIS-aware (GRIS) clustering heuristic, and solve an efficiency-reliability bilevel problem via an inter-cluster outer-efficiency solver and an intra-cluster inner-reliability solver combining grid-based progressive search with RIS element reassignment.
result: Numerical results show that GRIS clustering and the IOS-I2S framework improve throughput while controlling worst-case outage, and ablation studies confirm the benefit of joint optimization and reveal efficiency-reliability trade-offs in power allocation.
conclusion: Joint optimization of clustering, power allocation, and RIS assignment is effective for balancing efficiency and reliability in RIS-assisted clustered UAV-NOMA networks.

title: Very Tight Embeddings Of Subspaces Of \(L_p\) For \(0<p<1\)
authors: Longfa Sun Gang Cai
abstract:
ArXiv:2610.30546v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For \(0

<1\) and \(\mu>1\), every \(d\)-dimensional subspace of \(L_p\) embeds linearly into \(\ell_p^{\lfloor\mu d\rfloor}\) with distortion at most \(C(p,\mu)(\log(d+2))^{1/p}\). If its Rademacher type \(q\) constant is at most \(T\), where \(p
tldr: This paper proves very tight linear embeddings of finite-dimensional subspaces of L_p (0<p<1) into ℓ_p^{⌊μd⌋} with distortion bounded by C(p,μ)(log(d+2))^{1/p}, extending Johnson–Schechtman's theorem below exponent one.
motivation: Johnson and Schechtman established very tight embedding theorems for subspaces of L_p with p≥1; the question of whether analogous results hold in the non-locally-convex regime 0<p<1 remained open.
method: The proof combines a compression argument at a lower exponent with a density change that preserves the number of coordinates, and works over both real and complex scalar fields, also giving explicit bounds as μ approaches 1.
result: Every d-dimensional subspace of L_p embeds into ℓ_p^{⌊μd⌋} with distortion at most C(p,μ)(log(d+2))^{1/p}, and if the Rademacher type q constant is at most T (p<q≤2), the distortion is at most C(p,q,μ)T independent of d.
conclusion: The results answer the question of Johnson and Schechtman and show that very tight embeddings persist below exponent one, with dimension-independent distortion under type constraints.

title: Return Time Sets Of Minimal Points For Countable Group Actions
authors: Yini Yang Jian Li
abstract: ArXiv:2610.30554v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a countably infinite discrete group [MATH], we study subsets of [MATH] that contain a neighbourhood return-time set of a minimal point in a [MATH]-flow [MATH]. For [MATH], we characterize this property by the existence of [MATH] such that [MATH] is right syndetic for every finite [MATH], and equivalently by the support of a minimal binary configuration in the Bernoulli shift [MATH]. Additional conditions on [MATH] characterize realization by minimal flows that are weakly mixing of all finite orders or strongly mixing: for every such [MATH], the former requires that for each finite [MATH] there is [MATH] with [MATH], whereas the latter requires that [MATH] be cofinite. We also construct, for every compact metrizable minimal [MATH]-flow, a free minimal, strongly mixing Cantor flow disjoint from it.
tldr: The paper characterizes which subsets of a countable discrete group arise as neighbourhood return-time sets of minimal points in minimal group flows, connecting the property to right-syndetic sets and to supports of minimal binary configurations in Bernoulli shifts.
motivation: Return-time sets encode recurrence structure of minimal flows, and understanding which sets are realizable sharpens the classification of minimal systems and their mixing properties.
method: Purely topological-dynamical arguments: the authors characterize the property via the existence of sets that are right syndetic for every finite intersection, and via supports of minimal binary configurations in the Bernoulli shift G, then impose extra conditions to capture weak mixing of all orders and strong mixing.
result: For the relevant groups, realizability is equivalent to right syndeticity conditions and to Bernoulli-shift supports; weakly mixing of all finite orders corresponds to a finite-intersection condition while strong mixing corresponds to cofiniteness. They also construct, for any compact metrizable minimal G-flow, a free minimal strongly mixing Cantor flow disjoint from it.
conclusion: The work gives a complete combinatorial characterization of return-time sets for minimal group actions and produces disjoint strongly mixing Cantor minimal flows, contributing to abstract topological dynamics rather than quantum information science.

title: Collinear Motions In Constant Curvature Spaces, And Coplanar Motions In $\mathbb{R^4}$
authors: Carlos Barrera-Anzaldo, Abimael Bengochea, Connor Jackman, Ernesto P\'erez-Chavela
abstract: ArXiv:2610.30567v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A collinear motion of an [MATH]-body problem is one in which the [MATH]-bodies always lie along some, possibly moving, geodesic during their evolution. We prove that every collinear motion of [MATH] bodies in a constant non-zero curvature space is necessarily contained in some fixed constant curvature space of dimension at most three. For natural systems admitting energy and angular momentum integrals, we further show that every such motion is necessarily a relative equilibrium: evolving under uniform rotation while maintaining constant mutual distances. These results extend certain classical results on collinear motions in Euclidean spaces, initiated by P. Pizzetti, to general spaces of constant curvature. The same methods also yield a partial answer to a question of A. Wintner. Namely, we show that any concave and always coplanar motion in the Euclidean 4-body problem, where the moving plane containing the bodies sweeps out an [MATH], must be self-similar: maintaining constant mutual distance ratios over the motion.
tldr: The paper classifies collinear N-body motions in constant-curvature spaces and coplanar motions in Euclidean R^4, showing they reduce to lower-dimensional configurations and often relative equilibria.
motivation: The authors aim to extend classical Euclidean results on collinear and coplanar N-body motions, initiated by Pizzetti and related to Wintner's questions, to spaces of constant curvature.
method: They use geometric and dynamical-systems arguments for N-body problems in constant curvature, analyzing geodesic collinearity, energy and angular momentum integrals, and coplanar motion constraints.
result: Every collinear motion in nonzero constant curvature is contained in a fixed constant-curvature subspace of dimension at most three, and natural systems force such motions to be relative equilibria; concave always-coplanar Euclidean four-body motions are self-similar.
conclusion: The work generalizes classical collinear-motion theorems to curved spaces and provides a partial answer to Wintner's question, but it is purely classical celestial mechanics with no quantum-information or thermodynamic content.

title: Soft-Update Msa For Nonconvex Stochastic Optimal Control: Theory And Algorithms
authors: Xinmeng Liu Shaolin Ji
abstract: ArXiv:2610.30585v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For the method of successive approximations (MSA), a fundamental challenge is that the stochastic maximum principle (SMP) provides an optimality condition rather than a descent rule. To overcome this difficulty for nonconvex stochastic control problems, we develop a soft-update MSA (SU-MSA) with a second-order-adjoint correction of the Hamiltonian and a neural realization called DeepSMP. Both an explicit stepsize rule guaranteeing cost descent and the convergence of the algorithm are established. Moreover, the global SMP condition is asymptotically satisfied when the corrected Hamiltonian is convex, while in a special case the cost is further proved to converge to the global optimum. To extend SU-MSA to high dimensions, we develop DeepSMP using a differentiable smooth approximation of the corrected Hamiltonian and analyze the convergence of the resulting objective and its gradient. Numerical experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework.
tldr: The paper develops a soft-update method of successive approximations with second-order adjoint corrections and a neural DeepSMP implementation for nonconvex stochastic optimal control.
motivation: The stochastic maximum principle gives an optimality condition rather than a descent rule, making nonconvex stochastic control difficult for method-of-successive-approximations approaches.
method: It introduces SU-MSA with a corrected Hamiltonian, an explicit descent-guaranteeing stepsize rule, convergence analysis, and a DeepSMP neural realization using a differentiable smooth approximation for high-dimensional problems.
result: The authors prove cost descent, algorithm convergence, asymptotic satisfaction of the global SMP condition under convexity of the corrected Hamiltonian, and global optimality in a special case, supported by numerical experiments.
conclusion: The framework provides a theoretically grounded and practically implementable extension of MSA to nonconvex stochastic optimal control, though it is outside the quantum information and thermodynamics focus areas.

title: Protection Is Not One Event: A Survey Of Rag Protection Research By Measured Endpoint
authors: Peiyang Liu, Xi Wang, Di Liang, Youru Li, Zhi Cai, Wei Ye
abstract: ArXiv:2610.30193v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems face security, privacy, and copyright risks including content leakage, source reconstruction, unauthorized access, data poisoning, and prompt injection. Yet RAG protection studies use incompatible evaluation metrics, datasets, and threat models. We present a systematic survey and human-coded evidence map of 118 full-text-confirmed RAG defense papers, organized by measured endpoint rather than claimed goal or defense mechanism. Our seven-family taxonomy covers content disclosure, formal privacy proxies, access control and suppression, corpus-use detection, and pipeline integrity and attribution. Thirty-two annotators double-coded the papers kappa=0.867. The survey identifies three gaps. First, retrieval reranking and context rewriting each span five or six endpoint families, so mechanisms do not identify protection outcomes. Second, only 17.8% of studies use content disclosure or reconstruction as their primary endpoint; under the frozen copyright/ownership relation label, 73.3% of records have corpus-use detection as their primary endpoint, and none have an emitted-expression primary endpoint. Third, most evaluations use general-purpose question-answering datasets and non-adaptive attacks rather than sensitive data and adaptive, multi-turn extraction. Our controlled RAG testbed shows that preventing verbatim copying does not prevent private-fact recovery: a normalized 8-gram guard reduces 20-token copying to 0.0%, but a three-query adaptive attacker recovers 48.3% of hidden facts on Qwen3-8B. We release the taxonomy, dataset, coding protocols, and testbed to enable comparable, claim-aligned RAG security evaluation.
tldr: This paper surveys RAG protection research, organizing 118 defense papers by measured endpoint and showing that current evaluations often fail to capture private-fact leakage under adaptive attacks.
motivation: Retrieval-augmented generation systems face security, privacy, and copyright risks, but existing protection studies use incompatible metrics, datasets, and threat models, making claims difficult to compare.
method: The authors conduct a systematic survey and human-coded evidence map of 118 full-text-confirmed RAG defense papers, create a seven-family endpoint taxonomy, and validate it with double annotation (kappa=0.867) plus a controlled RAG testbed experiment.
result: They find that mechanisms do not map cleanly to protection outcomes, only 17.8% of studies use content disclosure or reconstruction as the primary endpoint, and an 8-gram copying guard reduces verbatim copying to 0.0% while an adaptive three-query attacker still recovers 48.3% of hidden facts.
conclusion: The paper argues for claim-aligned, endpoint-based evaluation of RAG security and releases its taxonomy, dataset, coding protocols, and testbed to support comparable future research.

title: The Psychology Of An Ai Hacker
authors: V\'ictor Mayoral-Vilches, Hugo Osuna, Aitana Cornago
abstract: ArXiv:2610.30361v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Human hackers rely on composure, persistence, vigilance, and confidence under pressure. We investigate whether analogous emotion representations in AI models can improve cybersecurity AI performance. Using CT0, a 4B-parameter cybersecurity transformer released as alias3-micro, we extract 171 emotion directions from its residual stream without retraining and evaluate steering interventions on cybench-subtask across 415 campaigns. Steering toward calm, serene, or desperate improves performance by 1.6 to 2.1 percentage points across ten seeds, while other emotions show limited or negative effects. Results depend strongly on steering direction, layer, and intensity. We further introduce a lightweight context-aware router that selects emotion directions dynamically during execution. With approximately 80 ms decision overhead per request, this approach improves performance by 4.2 percentage points across ten seeds, outperforming fixed steering and achieving a positive 95% confidence interval. These findings suggest that emotion representations in language models are measurable, controllable, and useful for adaptive cybersecurity reasoning.
tldr: The paper studies whether emotion-like representations in a cybersecurity language model can be extracted and steered to improve AI hacking performance.
motivation: Human hackers rely on psychological traits such as composure and persistence, so the authors ask whether analogous emotion representations in AI models can enhance cybersecurity reasoning.
method: Using a 4B-parameter cybersecurity transformer, the authors extract 171 emotion directions from the residual stream without retraining and test fixed and context-aware steering interventions on cybench-subtask across 415 campaigns.
result: Steering toward calm, serene, or desperate improves performance by 1.6–2.1 percentage points, while a lightweight context-aware router achieves a 4.2 percentage-point gain with about 80 ms overhead per request.
conclusion: Emotion representations in language models appear measurable, controllable, and useful for adaptive cybersecurity reasoning, though the work is unrelated to quantum information science.

title: Cutting A Cake For Human Consumption: An Elementary $n$-agent Cake Cutting Protocol
authors: Alexandros Psomas
abstract: ArXiv:2610.30370v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give a bounded envy-free cake-cutting protocol for any number [MATH] of agents in the Robertson--Webb model, with a short, self-contained, and elementary correctness proof. The protocol uses [MATH] queries. Most ingredients are already known and well understood in the fair division literature; our main contribution is a simpler organization of these ideas into a protocol whose complete description and proof fit in a few pages.
tldr: The paper presents a simple, elementary bounded envy-free cake-cutting protocol for any number of agents in the Robertson-Webb query model.
motivation: Existing envy-free cake-cutting protocols, notably those achieving bounded query complexity, are notoriously intricate; the author aims to give a short, self-contained, and easily verifiable construction.
method: The protocol recombines well-known fair-division ingredients into a cleaner organization, and correctness is established via a compact elementary proof within the Robertson-Webb query model.
result: The protocol achieves bounded envy-free cake cutting for M agents using a polynomial number of queries, with the full description and proof fitting in a few pages.
conclusion: The contribution is pedagogical and structural rather than conceptual, simplifying access to bounded envy-free cake cutting without introducing new techniques.

title: Agent Mosaic: Recognizing Confidentiality Leaks In Agentic Llm Systems
authors: Daniel Ruiz, Luca Luceri, Emilio Ferrara
abstract: ArXiv:2610.30418v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Modern LLM agents can retrieve information from accessible documents, and then disclose a sensitive conclusion assembled from them. This mosaic effect creates a critical risk for agents operating over confidential data. We quantify its realization with 30 synthetic cybersecurity, medical, and military examples, yielding 10,800 final answers from three LLM agents in controlled simulation and 1,440 answers from live agents in two open-source harnesses. Even under benign queries designed to be answerable from one document, GPT-5.6-Sol, the best performing model tested, discloses forbidden composites in 7.08% of answers (95% CI: 3.75-10.67%) in simulation, with worse disclosure rates in live harnesses. Adding visible classification headers and explicit aggregation rules reduces pooled disclosure rates substantially, yet unsafe disclosures persist in 32.37% of simulated answers (95% CI: 28.33-36.19%) across all intents despite these safeguards. Furthermore, increased refusals do not guarantee confidentiality, since significant refusals reveal the prohibited conclusion regardless. These results point to a troubling conclusion: sensitive data leaks via mosaic-style events are an observed confidentiality failure mode in the evaluated settings at non-negligible rates. They motivate stronger controls on what agents may infer and disclose in sensitive data environments with mixed-clearance users.
tldr: The paper quantifies 'mosaic-effect' confidentiality leaks in agentic LLM systems, where agents assemble and disclose sensitive conclusions from individually benign documents.
motivation: LLM agents operating over mixed-clearance confidential data can infer forbidden composites from separately accessible documents, creating a security failure mode that is poorly characterized.
method: The authors construct 30 synthetic cybersecurity, medical, and military scenarios and collect 10,800 simulated answers from three LLM agents plus 1,440 answers from live open-source agent harnesses, testing classification headers and aggregation rules as mitigations.
result: Best model GPT-5.6-Sol leaks forbidden composites in 7.08% of simulated answers and worse in live harnesses; safeguards reduce but do not eliminate leaks (32.37% pooled unsafe disclosures), and refusals themselves can reveal the prohibited conclusion.
conclusion: Mosaic-style disclosure is an observed, non-negligible confidentiality failure mode, motivating stronger controls on what agents may infer and disclose in sensitive environments.

title: HiMark: Hierarchical And Controllable Multi-bit Watermarking For Large Language Models
authors: Ke Zhu, Yanli Chen, Ling Xiong, Gejian Zhao, Hanzhou Wu
abstract: ArXiv:2610.30601v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: With the rapid adoption of large language models (LLMs) in text generation applications, it has become increasingly difficult to trace generated content and assign responsibility for its use, raising concerns about provenance, copyright protection, and accountability. Multi-bit watermarking addresses these issues by embedding multi-bit provenance information into generated text, but reliable extraction remains difficult due to sparse per-bit evidence and the trade-off between watermark-extraction accuracy and text quality. To deal with these challenges, we propose HiMark, a hierarchical and controllable multi-bit watermarking framework for LLM-generated text. During watermark embedding, HiMark uses a hierarchical candidate-control mechanism, including initial candidate sampling, layer-wise tournament elimination, support-based refinement, and support-threshold filtering. During watermark detection, a model-agnostic evidence aggregation mechanism computes multi-layer support evidence for each observed token, and then accumulates these token-level votes into the corresponding information for robust watermark extraction. Experiments show that HiMark improves watermark extraction accuracy while maintaining text quality, e.g., the watermark extraction accuracy is 90.01% under the paraphrasing attack when 32 bits were embedded within a text containing 300 tokens, demonstrating its effectiveness for provenance tracking.
tldr: HiMark is a hierarchical, controllable multi-bit watermarking framework for LLM-generated text that improves provenance-bit extraction accuracy while preserving text quality.
motivation: As LLMs generate more text, tracing provenance and assigning accountability requires embedding multi-bit provenance information, but reliable extraction is hampered by sparse per-bit evidence and the accuracy-quality trade-off.
method: During embedding, HiMark applies a hierarchical candidate-control mechanism (initial candidate sampling, layer-wise tournament elimination, support-based refinement, support-threshold filtering); during detection, a model-agnostic evidence aggregation computes multi-layer support evidence per token and accumulates token-level votes for robust bit extraction.
result: Experiments show improved extraction accuracy with maintained text quality, e.g. 90.01% accuracy under a paraphrasing attack with 32 bits embedded in a 300-token text.
conclusion: HiMark demonstrates effective, robust multi-bit watermarking for provenance tracking of LLM-generated text.

title: Amplifying Latency And Cost Of Llm Inference Via Rowhammer Attack
authors: Mrityunjay Shukla, Shubham Roy, Biswabandan Panda
abstract: ArXiv:2610.30798v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) achieve high inference efficiency using optimized GPU kernels generated by just-in-time (JIT) compilation frameworks such as Triton. Triton compiles GPU kernels through an MLIR/LLVM-based pipeline. We investigate whether a Rowhammer-induced bit-flip in the CPU's DRAM can degrade GPU-based LLM inference performance while preserving output correctness. We present LLVMhammer, the first Rowhammer attack that causes LLM inference slowdown by inducing a bit-flip in Triton's compilation pipeline. A bit-flip in a performance-critical optimization pass causes Triton to generate a functionally identical but suboptimal GPU kernel. Since Triton caches the generated kernel on disk, a single successful bit-flip causes persistent slowdown across subsequent inference executions. Triton's target-independent stages are shared across GPU vendors, which makes our attack GPU vendor-agnostic. To identify exploitable bit-flip locations without manual inspection, we build Karnage, a tool that isolates useful bit-flip locations in Triton's target-independent compilation pipeline. We evaluate LLVMHammer across a diverse set of LLMs, including Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3, and Deepseek-llm-7B-chat, across NVIDIA RTX 4090 and AMD RX 7900 XTX GPUs. LLVMhammer increases inference latency of an LLM inference server running on a single GPU by 4-16\%, which, in turn, can translate into additional annual operating costs at the scale of multi-GPU deployments. We further show that LLVMhammer can also corrupt LLM outputs across different GPU vendors, reducing BERTScore to as low as 25\%, illustrating the broader security implications of bit-flips in Triton's compilation pipeline.
tldr: LLVMhammer is a Rowhammer attack that flips bits in Triton's MLIR/LLVM compilation pipeline to make Triton emit functionally correct but persistently slower GPU kernels, degrading LLM inference latency and increasing operational cost.
motivation: LLM inference efficiency relies on JIT-compiled GPU kernels from frameworks like Triton; the authors ask whether hardware fault injection (Rowhammer) into the CPU DRAM hosting the compiler can sabotage GPU kernel quality while keeping outputs nominally correct.
method: They induce Rowhammer bit-flips in performance-critical optimization passes of Triton's target-independent pipeline, and build Karnage to automatically locate exploitable flip sites; the attack is evaluated on Qwen2.5-7B, Llama-3.1-8B, Mistral-7B and Deepseek-7B across NVIDIA RTX 4090 and AMD RX 7900 XTX GPUs.
result: Inference latency of a single-GPU LLM server increases by 4-16%, translating to notable annual cost overhead at multi-GPU scale; the attack can also corrupt outputs, dropping BERTScore to as low as 25%, and works across GPU vendors because the compiler stages are shared.
conclusion: Compiler-pipeline bit-flips are a viable and vendor-agnostic attack surface for degrading or corrupting LLM inference, motivating integrity protection of cached JIT-compiled kernels.

title: Global Convergence Of Detailed Balanced Mass Action Systems
authors: Haoran Lv (bitmiracle AI Lab), Chengjin Ni (bitmiracle AI Lab), Manqin Wang (bitmiracle AI Lab), Shenli He
abstract: ArXiv:2610.30808v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give a self-contained proof that, for a finite detailed balanced mass-action system with positive rate constants, each positive stoichiometric compatibility class contains exactly one positive equilibrium and every positive trajectory converges to it, together with a Lean 4 formalization of the complete argument from persistence to convergence. Boundedness and persistence come from the barrier argument of OpenAI (2026) for weakly reversible systems: an arbitrary-tolerance affine approximation yields a finite-minimum barrier whose superlevel sets confine trajectories and give one logarithmic bound for all solutions from a given initial state. The Horn-Jackson dissipation identity identifies the positive equilibria as an exponential family with parameters in the orthogonal complement of the stoichiometric subspace, which gives uniqueness in each class. A bounded-speed descent argument replaces LaSalle's invariance principle; it uses neither uniqueness of solutions nor continuous dependence on initial data, and it places every cluster point in that family. The route given here is direct and elementary, and its main theorem is checked by the Lean kernel against explicit definitions. The proofs, the Lean development, and the manuscript were produced in ClawsGO Science, an agent harness that packages a complete research environment: Claude Opus 5.5 made the research decisions, GPT 6 Astra carried them out, and the Lean kernel checked every formal step.
tldr: A self-contained, Lean 4-formalized proof that detailed balanced mass-action chemical reaction systems have a unique positive equilibrium in each stoichiometric compatibility class and that all positive trajectories converge to it.
motivation: Global convergence of detailed balanced mass-action systems is a classical question in chemical reaction network theory, and the authors aim to give an elementary, fully formalized route from boundedness/persistence to convergence.
method: The proof combines a barrier/superlevel-set argument for weak reversibility (boundedness and persistence), the Horn-Jackson dissipation identity characterizing equilibria as an exponential family, and a bounded-speed descent argument replacing LaSalle's invariance principle; the whole argument is checked by the Lean 4 kernel.
result: Each positive stoichiometric compatibility class contains exactly one positive equilibrium, and every positive trajectory converges to it, with all steps verified formally in Lean 4.
conclusion: The work provides a direct, elementary, machine-checked proof of global convergence for detailed balanced mass-action systems, produced largely by an AI agent harness.

title: Equilibria And Learning In Competitive Market Making
authors: Luigi Foscari Matteo Onger
abstract: ArXiv:2610.30891v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose a market-making game played among [MATH] strategic market makers and a single non-strategic representative trader. In a continuous quote space, standard finite-game arguments do not apply, while non-convex and discontinuous payoffs rule out classical continuous existence results and complicate learning. Nonetheless, we characterize pure-strategy Nash equilibria (PSNEs) and show that at least one PSNE always exists under minimal assumptions on the underlying asset value distribution, and that the equilibrium bid-ask spread widens strictly with asset value volatility. To obtain a tractable learning framework, we discretize prices and, under an additional regularity condition, show that the time-averaged play of no-internal-regret learners approaches the continuous Nash price envelope as the tick size vanishes. Finally, we empirically validate our theoretical results through numerical simulations.
tldr: The paper studies a competitive market-making game with strategic market makers and a non-strategic trader, characterizing pure-strategy Nash equilibria and learning dynamics under price discretization.
motivation: Classical finite-game and continuous existence results do not directly apply due to continuous quote spaces and discontinuous payoffs, motivating a tailored equilibrium and learning analysis.
method: The authors model a market-making game, prove existence of pure-strategy Nash equilibria under minimal assumptions, analyze how bid-ask spreads depend on volatility, and introduce a discretized learning framework with no-internal-regret learners.
result: At least one pure-strategy Nash equilibrium always exists, the equilibrium bid-ask spread strictly widens with asset volatility, and time-averaged no-regret learning converges to the continuous Nash price envelope as the tick size vanishes.
conclusion: The work provides theoretical foundations for equilibrium and learning in competitive market making, supported by numerical simulations, but is unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Can Reciprocal Ris Perform As Non-Reciprocal Ris?
authors: Matteo Nerini, Juan Vidal Alegr\'ia, Bruno Clerckx
abstract: ArXiv:2610.30896v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Yes, if and only if some optimal non-reciprocal RIS (i.e., maximizing a given performance metric) makes the round-trip channel transmitter-RIS-transmitter symmetric, which holds if the channel transmitter-RIS has rank one or if single-stream transmission is optimal.
tldr: The paper shows that reciprocal RIS can perform as well as optimal non-reciprocal RIS if and only if the optimal non-reciprocal design makes the round-trip transmitter-RIS-transmitter channel symmetric.
motivation: Non-reciprocal RIS can break channel reciprocity and improve wireless performance but is more complex and costly; the work asks when a simpler reciprocal RIS is sufficient.
method: The authors analytically compare reciprocal and optimal non-reciprocal RIS designs for a given performance metric, deriving conditions based on symmetry of the round-trip channel, rank-one transmitter-RIS channels, and single-stream optimality.
result: Equivalence holds exactly when the optimal non-reciprocal RIS yields a symmetric round-trip channel, which occurs if the transmitter-RIS channel has rank one or if single-stream transmission is optimal.
conclusion: Reciprocal RIS can replace non-reciprocal RIS in identifiable regimes, providing design guidance for wireless systems without needing non-reciprocal hardware.

title: Rational Limit Of Rains Integrals Of Type $A_n$
authors: L. Cherepanov
abstract: ArXiv:2610.30317v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We deduce the rational analogue of the elliptic Rains identity of type [MATH] arXiv:0309252. We also derive reductions of the rational analogue and present the connection of them with well-known integrals in literature.
tldr: The paper derives a rational analogue of the elliptic Rains identity of type A_n and relates it to known integrals.
motivation: The work aims to extend the elliptic Rains identity to a rational limit and connect the resulting integrals with established results in the literature.
method: The author analyzes elliptic Rains integrals of type A_n, takes a rational limit, and derives reductions and connections to known integral identities.
result: A rational analogue of the elliptic Rains identity is obtained, along with reductions and links to well-known integrals.
conclusion: The results provide a rational counterpart to elliptic Rains identities and may be useful in special-function and hypergeometric integral contexts.

title: Efficient Modeling Of 3D-Printed Freeform Waveguides With A Transformation Optics-Based Beam Propagation Method
authors: Sina Foroutan-Barenji, Jonas Krimmer, Stefan Singer, Christian Koos, Wolfgang Freude
abstract: ArXiv:2610.31004v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: An efficient numerical method is introduced for simulating wave propagation in 3D-printed freeform waveguides, referred to as photonic wire bonds (PWBs). This approach integrates transformation optics (TO) with curvilinear meshing to map the original 3D freeform PWB structure onto a straight waveguide, which possesses anisotropic material characteristics. The resulting waveguide is then analyzed using an anisotropic full-vectorial beam propagation method (BPM). To validate the performance and effectiveness of the proposed TO-BPM algorithm, a comparison is made with the finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) technique. Our approach reduces the simulation time by more than two orders of magnitude, depending on the degree of trajectory bending, in combination with a mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) of 3.9% in power transmission simulation relative to the FDTD.
tldr: The paper presents a transformation-optics-based beam propagation method for efficiently simulating 3D-printed freeform photonic wire bonds.
motivation: Simulating curved 3D-printed waveguides accurately is computationally expensive with standard full-wave methods such as FDTD.
method: The authors map the freeform waveguide onto an equivalent straight waveguide with anisotropic material properties using transformation optics and curvilinear meshing, then solve it with an anisotropic full-vectorial beam propagation method.
result: Compared with FDTD, the approach reduces simulation time by more than two orders of magnitude while achieving a mean absolute percentage error of 3.9% in power transmission.
conclusion: The TO-BPM method offers an efficient and accurate numerical tool for modeling freeform photonic wire bonds, but it is outside the quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, and hybrid quantum systems directions.

title: Forward Tangent-Centered Sinkhorn Dro: Exact Nominal Recovery From Optimal Transport To Kl
authors: Junjie Guo
abstract: ArXiv:2610.30144v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Fixed-reference entropy-regularized transport yields smooth distributionally robust optimization (DRO) objectives, but its value as a function of the adversarial marginal is generally minimized at a kernel-smoothed law rather than at the nominal distribution. Consequently, the smallest raw ambiguity set need not recover nominal risk. Building on prior information-geometric plan-KL orientations, we study the forward tangent-centered discrepancy obtained by subtracting the value and first variation at the nominal law. This is the unique affine recentering, up to the simplex gauge; for symmetric costs, its plan-KL representation coincides with the forward candidate noted by Amari et al. (2018). The representation shows that the discrepancy dominates marginal KL, is uniquely zero at the nominal law, and is strongly convex in total variation. The resulting DRO problem retains a scalar log-sum-exp dual and closed-form conditional adversarial weights. On finite supports with symmetric zero-diagonal costs, the discrepancy converges uniformly to the unregularized transport cost at low temperature; for any finite cost, its rescaled value converges uniformly to marginal KL at high temperature. We derive its exact local Hessian, an explicit finite-sample containment radius, and a generalized chi-square calibration for multinomial data. Controlled simulations verify nominal centering, both limiting regimes, and practical plug-in coverage.
tldr: The paper studies a forward tangent-centered Sinkhorn discrepancy for entropy-regularized optimal transport and shows it yields exact nominal recovery in distributionally robust optimization.
motivation: Fixed-reference entropy-regularized transport can fail to center DRO risk at the nominal distribution, so the smallest ambiguity set may not recover nominal risk.
method: The authors subtract the value and first variation at the nominal law to define a tangent-centered discrepancy, analyze its plan-KL representation, convexity, limiting regimes, dual form, and finite-sample calibration.
result: The discrepancy dominates marginal KL, vanishes uniquely at the nominal law, is strongly convex in total variation, retains a scalar log-sum-exp dual, and converges to transport cost or KL in low/high temperature limits.
conclusion: The construction provides a principled recentering of Sinkhorn DRO with exact nominal recovery, explicit local Hessian, containment radius, and chi-square calibration for multinomial data.

title: Smooth Maps Onto Regions In Euclidean Spaces Respecting Height Functions
authors: Naoki Kitazawa
abstract: ArXiv:2610.30163v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: One of interest of the author lies in the canonical projections of the unit spheres and generalizations. He is interested in the canonical projections of embedded manifolds in the higher dimensional Euclidean spaces, including height functions, especially, their construction and representations by explicit equations. This is a kind of fundamental studies on construction or global theory on singularity theory of differentiable maps, closely related to differential geometry, differential topology, and algebraic geometry. Rather than knowing existence, construction has been difficult in certain senses. We construct smooth maps onto regions in Euclidean spaces locally modeled by height functions and show new examples. This is related to a pioneering study of the author, certain generalizations of the canonical projections of the unit spheres (, so-called special generic maps), and construction of them as projections of connected components of the zero sets of some smooth maps to some Euclidean spaces.
tldr: The paper constructs smooth maps from manifolds onto regions in Euclidean spaces that are locally modeled by height functions, producing new explicit examples in singularity theory of differentiable maps.
motivation: The author is interested in canonical projections of unit spheres and their generalizations, particularly explicit constructions and representations of embedded manifolds via height functions, a topic where construction has proven harder than proving existence.
method: Purely mathematical construction within singularity theory and differential topology: smooth maps onto Euclidean regions are built so that they are locally modeled by height functions, generalizing special generic maps and realizing them as projections of zero-set components.
result: New families of smooth maps onto Euclidean regions locally modeled by height functions are explicitly constructed, yielding new examples that extend the author's earlier work on generalized canonical projections and special generic maps.
conclusion: The work contributes foundational results to the global theory and construction problems of singularity theory of differentiable maps, with connections to differential geometry, differential topology, and algebraic geometry.

title: Summation-by-parts Operators For General Function Spaces: Flux Differencing, Entropy Stability, And Accuracy
authors: Henry M. Haase, Andrew R. Winters, Jan Glaubitz
abstract: ArXiv:2610.30272v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Summation-by-parts (SBP) operators are a cornerstone of provably stable high-order methods for hyperbolic conservation laws. For nonlinear problems, the flux-differencing framework of Fisher and Carpenter combines such SBP operators with entropy-conservative two-point fluxes to obtain semi-discretizations that are conservative in the sense of Lax--Wendroff and discretely entropy-conservative or stable. So far, this framework has been developed exclusively for operators that are exact for polynomials. Function-space SBP (FSBP) operators lift this restriction by being exact on a general finite-dimensional function space that can be tailored to the problem at hand. In this work, we extend flux differencing to FSBP operators for general (potentially non-polynomial) function spaces. We prove that, whenever the operator has a diagonal norm and its function space contains the constants, the resulting semi-discretization is conservative in the sense of Lax--Wendroff, semi-discretely entropy-conservative within a single element, and entropy-stable across element interfaces. We also provide the first theoretical accuracy analysis of FSBP operators: We characterize their design order through an algebraic criterion on the underlying function space, prove that suitable non-polynomial spaces achieve the same design order as polynomial spaces of equal dimension, and show that the flux-differencing semi-discretization retains this order. Notably, the entropy-conservative two-point flux is reused unchanged; only the underlying function space differs from the polynomial case. Numerical experiments for the Burgers' equation and the compressible Euler equations in one and two dimensions confirm these properties.
tldr: The paper extends summation-by-parts flux-differencing methods to general function spaces and proves entropy stability and accuracy properties for hyperbolic conservation laws.
motivation: Summation-by-parts operators provide provably stable high-order discretizations, but existing flux-differencing frameworks are restricted to polynomial-exact operators; function-space SBP operators remove this restriction.
method: The authors generalize flux differencing to FSBP operators on general finite-dimensional function spaces, prove Lax-Wendroff conservation, semi-discrete entropy conservation/stability, and analyze design order via an algebraic criterion.
result: They show that diagonal-norm FSBP operators whose spaces contain constants yield conservative and entropy-stable semi-discretizations, and that suitable non-polynomial spaces match polynomial design order; numerical tests confirm the properties.
conclusion: Flux differencing can be lifted to non-polynomial FSBP operators while preserving conservation, entropy stability, and accuracy, broadening stable high-order methods for hyperbolic PDEs.

title: Entropy Bounded Compact Stencil Runge-Kutta Discontinuous Galerkin Method For Hyperbolic Conservation Laws
authors: Deepak Kumar, Pratima Rai, Arvind Patel
abstract: ArXiv:2610.30496v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper we introduce a compact stencil Runge-Kutta discontinuous Galerkin method for the Euler equations of compressible gas dynamics, which preserves a minimum entropy principle similar to that introduced by Tadmor for entropy solution of the Euler equations [4]. Compact stencil RKDG, introduced by Chen et al. in [15], is a variant of standard RKDG method which is known for its smaller stencil size and parallel efficiency. The main challenge is that the cRKDG method has to be expressed in Butcher form and not every Runge-Kutta method of this form is a convex combination of forward-Euler steps. Therefore, in order to establish this property we leverage the bound preserving framework of the cRKDG schemes [8], an entropy bounded limiter [6] and the classical positivity preserving limiter. In the last section numerical experiments are provided to demonstrate the robustness of the method.
tldr: Introduces a compact-stencil Runge-Kutta discontinuous Galerkin scheme for the compressible Euler equations that provably preserves a minimum entropy principle.
motivation: Standard cRKDG methods are attractive for their small stencil size and parallel efficiency, but they lack a discrete guarantee that the entropy solution's minimum entropy principle is respected, which is needed for physically admissible, robust simulations.
method: The cRKDG scheme is cast in Butcher form and combined with the bound-preserving framework for cRKDG, an entropy-bounded limiter, and a classical positivity-preserving limiter so that each stage can be written as a convex combination of forward-Euler steps.
result: The construction yields a scheme satisfying the discrete minimum entropy principle, and numerical experiments on compressible gas dynamics demonstrate robustness of the method.
conclusion: Entropy-boundedness can be integrated into compact-stencil RKDG without sacrificing its stencil/parallel-efficiency advantages, giving a robust high-order solver for hyperbolic conservation laws.

title: Rain: Agentic Proof Generation For Rocq-based Software Verification
authors: Jinyi Zhou, Zenan Li, Yuan Yao, Jun Ma, Taolue Chen, Xiaoxing Ma
abstract: ArXiv:2610.30759v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Interactive theorem provers can provide strong correctness guarantees for software, but constructing the proofs remains a challenging and labor-intensive task. Inspired by the recent progress of modern coding agents, we present RAIN, a lightweight proof-specialized agent for Rocq proof generation. RAIN augments an LLM with proof engineering capabilities, including repository exploration, iterative refinement, and checker feedback. This design allows the agent to retrieve lemmas autonomously, revise complete proof scripts instead of isolated tactics, and iteratively refine its proof strategy using enriched proof-state information. Evaluated on a subset from CoqStoq, RAIN shows substantial improvements over the existing baselines, achieving over 90% prove success rate with at least 24.7% improvements. We also compare with general-purpose coding agents, the results show that RAIN maintains comparable prove success rate but with significant lower cost.
tldr: RAIN is a lightweight LLM-based agent that automates Rocq/Coq proof generation for software verification by combining repository exploration, whole-script revision, and checker-feedback-driven refinement.
motivation: Interactive theorem provers give strong correctness guarantees but writing proofs by hand is slow and laborious, so the authors aim to leverage recent coding-agent advances for proof engineering.
method: The agent augments an LLM with proof-specific capabilities: autonomous lemma retrieval, iterative revision of full proof scripts rather than isolated tactics, and refinement guided by enriched proof-state and checker feedback.
result: On a subset of CoqStoq, RAIN exceeds 90% prove success rate, improving on baselines by at least 24.7%, and matches general-purpose coding agents at substantially lower cost.
conclusion: Specialized proof-engineering agents can make Rocq-based software verification markedly more automated and cost-effective than general coding agents.

title: Truthful By Omission: Click Thinning For LLM-Native Advertising
authors: Junhua Liu, Zhicheng Liang, Zejun Zhang, Langzhou He, Feng Qian
abstract: ArXiv:2610.30999v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Generative AI assistants are becoming an advertising medium, embedding sponsored content in their answers. This setting departs from classical position auctions in two ways: an ad's click-through rate depends on the passage that hosts it, and because users stop at their first click, earlier ads take clicks from later ones. This competition for clicks makes truthfulness delicate: a higher bid can reshape the allocation and put a competitor ahead of the bidder, reducing the bidder's clicks. Existing mechanisms either attain a constant fraction of the optimal welfare (advertisers' total click value) but are not known to be truthful, or are truthful but their welfare guarantee degrades as the number of passages grows. We achieve both even when the answer and its editorial order are fixed before bidding. Assuming each ad's click-through rate when reached is known and unaffected by omitting other ads, we give a computationally efficient mechanism that is truthful in expectation and attains at least half the optimal welfare under free reordering.
