method: An LLM agent starts from an empty rule set and iteratively evolves human-readable Joern queries, guided solely by a second LLM critic that inspects flagged and unflagged code to propose fixes for false alarms and suspected misses, with no access to ground-truth labels.
result: On the OWASP Python Benchmark SESAA achieves a mean F1 of 0.742 across 8 runs, exceeding default configurations of five widely used tools and matching the best of them when that tool is tuned with ground-truth labels; in a pilot on real Python projects, pre-vulnerability-induced queries detected 10 of 19 subsequent CVEs.
conclusion: LLM agents can convert static-analysis rule maintenance from manual authoring into an automated iterative discovery-and-repair loop, yielding auditable executable queries engineers can inspect, modify, and run.

title: PhishGen: Understanding Llm Capabilities In Automated Phishing Website Generation
authors: Fujiao Ji, Yerim Kim, Yena Cho, Seonhye Park, Hyoungshick Kim, Doowon Kim
abstract: ArXiv:2610.30226v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Phishing relies on visual deception, traditionally requiring web-development skills or pre-built kits. LLMs erode this barrier by generating functional websites from natural-language prompts, yet prior work does not answer how far LLM-driven generation actually reaches: functionality is assessed by inspection rather than execution; visual fidelity is scored by automated metrics or a few internal coders rather than the humans such pages aim to deceive; evaluation is confined to commercial models; and no study benchmarks generated pages against phishing kits deployed in the wild. We present PhishGen, a framework that evaluates the appearance fidelity and end-to-end functionality of LLM-generated phishing pages. PhishGen constructs prompts across three input modalities in seven combinations with twelve safeguard-bypassing rewriting strategies, generates pages using 14 LLMs spanning commercial, open-source, and uncensored categories, and assesses each via automated similarity metrics, reference-based detectors, a crowdsourced user study, and execution-based functionality testing, benchmarking all results against 64 real-world phishing kits. Although 96.2% of safeguard-bypassing outputs render, their perceived fidelity is modest (2.02/5), and only 38.7% complete the full credential-harvesting pipeline, with the Unsaved error as the largest failure mode. Contrary to the belief that uncensored models pose the greatest threat, GPT 4.1 reaches 86.3 to 94.1% functional success while uncensored models rarely exceed 45.4%. Phishing kits remain more complete per sample, yet three strong LLMs surpass the kit-level rate (70.9 to 89.7%), showing that LLMs trade average completeness for scalable, low-barrier generation of working phishing pages. We further identify generator-level fingerprints that current similarity-based defenses miss, and distill recommendations for hybrid detectors.
tldr: PhishGen is a benchmarking framework that measures how well 14 commercial, open-source, and uncensored LLMs can generate functional and visually convincing phishing websites, comparing them against 64 real-world phishing kits.
motivation: LLMs lower the barrier to creating phishing pages, but prior evaluations relied on manual inspection, automated visual metrics, or commercial models only, leaving open how far LLM-driven phishing generation actually reaches and how it compares to deployed phishing kits.
method: The authors build prompts across three input modalities in seven combinations with twelve safeguard-bypassing rewriting strategies, generate pages with 14 LLMs, and evaluate them via similarity metrics, reference-based detectors, a crowdsourced user fidelity study, and execution-based end-to-end credential-harvesting tests benchmarked against 64 real phishing kits.
result: 96.2% of safeguard-bypassing outputs render but perceived fidelity is modest (2.02/5) and only 38.7% complete the full credential-harvesting pipeline; GPT-4.1 achieves 86.3-94.1% functional success while uncensored models rarely exceed 45.4%, and three strong LLMs surpass the kit-level success rate.
conclusion: LLMs trade average completeness for scalable, low-barrier generation of working phishing pages, and generator-level fingerprints are identified to inform hybrid defenses that current similarity-based detectors miss.

title: Data-Void Exploits In Web-Searching LLMs
authors: Michele Guerra, Wuyeh Jobe, Sanjana Nambiar, Christina P\"opper, Azza Abouzied
abstract: ArXiv:2610.30365v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Web-searching Large Language Models (LLMs) have changed how users seek online information: instead of sifting through ranked lists of links, users read synthesized answers. This shift creates a new LLM vulnerability: a data-void exploit. Disinformers publish their narratives in search spaces where relevant and reliable content is scarce, i.e. data voids, then rely on the LLM's web-search to retrieve and then use, cite, or list those pages in its responses to data-void seeking prompts. Unlike classical search, where users see ranking cues and competing results, LLMs can obscure when an answer relies on sparse, unverified, or adversarial sources. We study this threat by varying the user's prompt tone - skeptical, excited, or neutral - and LLM choice - ChatGPT, Gemini, or Sonar Pro - as well as three attacker controls. The attacker can use one of five known strategies to construct and fill a data void with their narrative, host their content at varying levels of visibility from well-established, indexed domains to less established ones, and include generative-optimization engine features thought to boost citing by web-searching LLMs. We find that data-void exploits can succeed with only a single attacker controlled page. Across all conditions, attacker-content appears in LLM responses 31% of the time. User controls offer limited protection: while skeptical prompts slightly reduce success and slightly increase flagging or warnings in LLM responses, we find no evidence of large effects of prompt tone or model choice on success rates, although smaller effects cannot be ruled out. Overall, our results establish data voids as a practical inference-time attack surface for manipulating web-searching LLMs through strategically placed web content and highlight the urgent need for defenses against such exploits.
tldr: The paper identifies and empirically evaluates 'data-void exploits', an inference-time attack in which adversaries plant content in sparse search spaces so that web-searching LLMs retrieve, cite, or repeat their narratives.
motivation: Web-searching LLMs replace ranked link lists with synthesized answers, hiding when responses rest on sparse or adversarial sources; disinformers can therefore exploit topical data voids, and the extent of this vulnerability was unquantified.
method: The authors vary prompt tone (skeptical, excited, neutral), LLM choice (ChatGPT, Gemini, Sonar Pro), void-construction strategy, hosting visibility, and generative-engine-optimization features, measuring how often attacker content appears in responses.
result: Attacker content appears in LLM responses in 31% of conditions, with a single attacker-controlled page sometimes sufficient; skeptical prompts give only a slight reduction in success and modest increase in flagging, and no large effects of tone or model choice were found.
conclusion: Data voids constitute a practical inference-time attack surface for manipulating web-searching LLMs, motivating defenses against strategically placed adversarial web content.

title: Temporal Liquidity Crossing For Blockchains: An Eip-1559 Extension For Admission Below The Base Fee
authors: Duanyang Dan Guo
abstract: ArXiv:2610.30595v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Transactions differ in how their value changes with execution time and relative position. Ethereum's EIP-1559 lets them compete through fee fields, but a fee bid gives no enforceable claim to an earlier position in the block, and no way to express willingness to accept a later one. Its base fee is a hard admission floor. We introduce temporal liquidity markets (TLM), a framework for crossing complementary temporal requirements: transactions seeking early-region execution (consumers) can fund transactions that opt into exclusion from that region (providers). Selected consumers complete within the early region and are ordered among themselves by authorization density, both validator-checked. In our block-local EIP-1559 extension, providers may be admitted below the base-fee floor. Under TLM regulation, funding-conditioned and capacity-capped provider gas is excluded from the ordinary EIP-1559 controller input. Counting it there instead raises the base fee and displaces ordinary demand at a positive base-fee fixed point. Exclusion lets the controller regulate ordinary demand at its original target and preserves the no-TLM ordinary allocation by construction; in synthetic experiments it raises total utilization with funded gas. Selected consumers pay their signed authorizations, which fund provider shortfalls; the surplus is burned. We state an adversary model with strategic senders and builders and prove eight properties under it, among them validator-checked rule validity, full burn of the base fee, and no subsidy. An inserted consumer bid cannot raise any other consumer's charge. With a provider fee-cap floor, a small, capped inclusion fee and a consumer allowance tied to funded provider gas by a large enough link ratio, no finite set of consumer bids or providers that the builder inserts raises its direct fee payoff.
tldr: The paper proposes temporal liquidity markets (TLM), an EIP-1559 extension that lets blockchain transactions trade execution-position preferences so providers can be admitted below the base-fee floor.
motivation: Ethereum's EIP-1559 fee bidding gives no enforceable claim to an earlier block position and imposes a hard base-fee admission floor, preventing transactions from expressing willingness to be delayed.
method: The authors define complementary consumer/provider temporal requirements, validator-checked ordering by authorization density, and a block-local EIP-1559 controller modification that excludes funding-conditioned provider gas from the base-fee input, analyzed under an adversary model with strategic senders and builders.
result: They prove eight properties including rule validity, full base-fee burn, and no subsidy, and show via synthetic experiments that total utilization rises with funded gas while the no-TLM allocation is preserved.
conclusion: TLM provides an incentive-compatible mechanism for temporal liquidity crossing in blockchains, but the work lies entirely outside quantum information science.

title: Model-intrinsic, Weight-level, And Training-free Spectral Fingerprinting For Large Language Models
authors: Yanan He, Yanli Chen, Ling Xiong, Gejian Zhao, Hanzhou Wu
abstract: ArXiv:2610.30626v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The increasing release and reuse of Large Language Models (LLMs) as open-weight checkpoints make model fingerprinting important for ownership protection and offline auditing. Existing fingerprinting methods typically construct evidence from query responses, generated outputs, or input-induced activations. Although effective in representation-based settings, they can be affected by prompt selection, decoding configuration, inference environment, and forward-pass implementation, which may limit their applicability. Here we introduce a model-intrinsic weight-level framework that derives compact fingerprints from spectral structures encoded in LLM parameters. Specifically, the framework constructs GATE spectral scalar features from the singular-value distributions of GATE projection weights in gated feed-forward networks (FFNs), and aggregates the resulting layer-wise features through depth-wise segmented pooling to form a model-level fingerprint. Such representation preserves coarse layer-depth organization while reducing dependence on strict layer-to-layer alignment, enabling comparison across LLMs with different depths. The similarity between fingerprints is computed by linear centered kernel alignment. The entire pipeline is training-free and does not require input samples, generated outputs, forward activations, or an auxiliary verifier. Experiments on representative LLM families and post-training variants have demonstrated a clear separation between source-related models and unrelated ones, and stable similarity under instruction tuning, quantization, pruning, and distillation-related modifications, which verify that spectral features are robust evidence for LLM fingerprinting.
tldr: A training-free, weight-level spectral fingerprinting framework for identifying and comparing large language models from the singular-value structure of their gated feed-forward projection weights.
motivation: As open-weight LLM checkpoints are increasingly released and reused, ownership protection and offline auditing require fingerprinting that does not depend on prompt selection, decoding settings, or inference-environment specifics, which limit response- or activation-based methods.
method: The authors extract GATE spectral scalar features from singular-value distributions of GATE projection weights in gated FFNs, aggregate layer-wise features via depth-wise segmented pooling into a model-level fingerprint, and compare fingerprints using linear centered kernel alignment.
result: Experiments across LLM families and post-training variants show clear separation between source-related and unrelated models, with stable similarity under instruction tuning, quantization, pruning, and distillation.
conclusion: Spectral features of weight matrices provide robust, model-intrinsic evidence for LLM fingerprinting without requiring inputs, outputs, activations, or auxiliary verifiers.

title: Your Token Is Gone: A Token-Consumption Countermeasure For Disrupting LLM-Based Scam Systems
authors: Fudu Xing, Kailong Wang, Tianlong Yu
abstract: ArXiv:2610.30666v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: LLM-based scam systems increasingly combine adaptive dialogue, persistent context, external tools, and multi-agent coordination to automate personalized fraud. These capabilities also create a resource dependency: every reasoning step, model call, and coordination round incurs inference cost. We present TokenTrap, a resource-oriented defense that redirects suspected scam systems toward benign, low-value computation while withholding credentials, payments, and other exploitable information. TokenTrap combines three components: an architecture-specific token-task library, a router that selects among single-agent, hierarchical, and flat multi-agent workflows, and a bounded anti-guardrail strategy that varies task presentation while enforcing token, round, time, and safety limits. Across 50-round traces, TokenTrap amplifies token consumption by [MATH], [MATH], and [MATH] relative to a no-token-task baseline for the three workflows. Its router achieves 85.67% accuracy on 300 architecture-labeled prompts. These results demonstrate that short, non-sensitive requests can impose substantial context-processing and coordination costs, motivating resource-aware defense as a complement to scam detection.
tldr: TokenTrap is a defensive countermeasure that drains the inference budget of LLM-based scam systems by routing them into benign, token-expensive tasks.
motivation: LLM-driven scam operations rely on iterative reasoning, tool calls, and multi-agent coordination, each of which costs tokens; the authors argue this resource dependency can be exploited as a defense surface.
method: The system combines an architecture-specific token-task library, a router that classifies the scammer's workflow (single-agent, hierarchical, flat multi-agent) with 85.67% accuracy, and a bounded anti-guardrail strategy that varies task presentation under token, round, time, and safety limits.
result: Over 50-round traces, TokenTrap amplifies token consumption substantially relative to a no-token-task baseline across all three workflow architectures while withholding credentials and payments.
conclusion: Short, non-sensitive requests can impose large context-processing and coordination costs, motivating resource-aware defense as a complement to conventional scam detection.

title: Fast Iterative Combinatorial Auctions Via Deep Reinforcement Learning
authors: Luis F. Paul Tosta, Quinn Arnold, Gianluca Brero
abstract: ArXiv:2610.30667v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Iterative combinatorial auctions are used in spectrum allocation, transportation, and industrial procurement, but rounds are costly. We introduce FastCombo, a deep reinforcement learning approach to sequential price discovery. Bayesian pricing has sharply reduced auction rounds even against subgradient benchmarks tuned with hindsight for each instance, but relies on a one-step objective and repeated online inference and optimization. We prove that greedily maximizing immediate clearing probability can require arbitrarily more rounds in expectation than an informative policy, even with the true valuation distribution known. FastCombo learns price policies offline, assigning credit to queries for the future decisions they enable and producing each online price update with a single neural-network forward pass. We formulate the objective of minimizing expected rounds to clearing in single-minded auctions as a partially observable Markov decision process and train a recurrent bidder-item graph policy over complete auction trajectories. In a one-item experiment, all five trained policies learn an informative opening, reducing expected rounds from 1.85 to 1.65 relative to the tested Bayesian one-step rule. Across four domains from the Combinatorial Auction Test Suite, FastCombo achieves competitive clearing while reducing measured online price-selection time per auction by a factor of roughly 300-900 relative to the standard Bayesian baseline. These results demonstrate the value of learning sequential price policies for both information acquisition and online computational efficiency.
tldr: FastCombo learns offline deep reinforcement learning policies for sequential price discovery in iterative combinatorial auctions, cutting online price-selection time by 300-900x versus Bayesian baselines.
motivation: Iterative combinatorial auctions suffer from costly rounds, and existing Bayesian one-step pricing rules are myopic and require repeated online inference and optimization.
method: The authors prove greedy immediate-probability maximization can be arbitrarily suboptimal, then formulate round-minimization in single-minded auctions as a POMDP and train a recurrent bidder-item graph policy over complete auction trajectories.
result: Trained policies discover informative openings in a one-item experiment, lowering expected rounds from 1.85 to 1.65, and remain competitive on four CATS domains while reducing per-auction price-selection time by roughly 300-900x.
conclusion: Learning sequential price policies jointly improves information acquisition and online computational efficiency in auction design.

title: Airo: A Streaming-Based Machine Learning Framework For Threat Detection And Security In Industrial Internet Of Things
authors: Raima Deb, Pranav M Pawar, Mithun Mukherjee, Raja Muthalagu, Mian Guo
abstract: ArXiv:2610.30713v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Modern Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) im- plementations now connect edge gateways, cloud dashboards and business applications. This improves visibility and remote monitoring. However it simultaneously exposes industrial traffic to various cyber threats including scanning, web attacks and Structured Query Language (SQL) injection (SQLi), phishing- driven credential theft, and command-and-control (C2) activity. Although rule-based tools remain useful for detecting known signatures, their efficacy decreases with minimally altered attacks or when alerts require manual investigation. This paper presents AIRO (Autonomous Intelligence-Driven Cybersecurity Risk Re- duction System), an efficient framework for IIoT monitoring and response. AIRO combines Apache Kafka streaming, attack- specific feature extraction, machine learning (ML) inference, confidence-based decision logic and risk reduction measures such as Internet Protocol (IP) blocking, account suspension and traffic limiting. We developed four specialized datasets for C2 beaconing, reconnaissance, SQLi, and phishing to evaluate AIRO. These datasets include noisy and overlapping characteristic distribu- tions to minimize label leakage. The best-performing models, primarily Gradient Boosting and LightGBM, achieve F1-scores up to 0.9229 while ensuring low-latency from event input to mitigation.
tldr: AIRO is a streaming machine-learning framework combining Apache Kafka, attack-specific feature extraction, and gradient-boosting/LightGBM classifiers to detect and mitigate cyber threats in Industrial IoT deployments.
motivation: IIoT environments connecting edge gateways, cloud dashboards, and business applications are exposed to scanning, SQL injection, phishing credential theft, and command-and-control traffic, and rule-based signature tools degrade against minimally altered attacks and alert floods.
method: The authors build four specialized datasets (C2 beaconing, reconnaissance, SQLi, phishing) with noisy and overlapping feature distributions to limit label leakage, then pipeline streaming ingestion through attack-specific feature extraction, ML inference, confidence-based decision logic, and automated mitigation such as IP blocking, account suspension, and traffic limiting.
result: Gradient Boosting and LightGBM models reach F1-scores up to 0.9229 while keeping end-to-end latency from event input to mitigation low.
conclusion: AIRO demonstrates that a streaming, ML-driven pipeline can provide practical, low-latency threat detection and automated response for industrial IoT networks.

title: NN-Based Transistor Modeling For Ultra-Fast Spice Simulation And Standard Cell Library Characterization
authors: Hussam Amrouch Rodion Novkin
abstract: ArXiv:2610.31024v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Neural network (NN)-based transistor models have proven to be a promising solution to accelerate device modeling. Although these models demonstrated remarkable speedup in circuit simulations, they were not rigorously tested in complex tasks within standard EDA tool flows for chip design, which require very high transistor model precision to provide accurate results and converge properly. To investigate their full potential and promise, we develop NN-based transistor models that accurately predict the drain current and various charges for a 3nm nanosheet, and employ the models for a standard cell library characterization. This enables us to evaluate the accuracy and speedup under a very wide range of SPICE simulations, benchmarking our models against an industry-standard implementation. Since standard cell library characterization involves thousands of SPICE simulations, it serves as a great benchmark for transistor model quality and consistency. To further evaluate model accuracy, we also perform analog- and digital-level simulations for various complex circuits. Our experiments reveal that NN-based models are a valid alternative to existing transistor compact models, capable of producing accurate delay and power estimates with a much higher speed and convergence time compared to the conventional Verilog-A-based industry-standard (BSIM-CMG) transistor compact model. Our NNs achieve sub-0.11% and 0.76% errors for delay and total power evaluation on a wide range of circuits, while taking up to 8 times less time during the standard cell library characterization. Additionally, we provide comprehensive information and guidance on NN accuracy, unveiling the relationship between NN size and its effect on circuit simulation precision.
tldr: The paper develops neural-network-based transistor models for 3nm nanosheet devices and benchmarks them against the industry-standard BSIM-CMG compact model in standard cell library characterization and circuit simulations.
motivation: NN-based transistor models promise speedups for device and circuit modeling, but they had not been rigorously validated in complex standard EDA flows requiring high precision and reliable convergence.
method: The authors train NN models to predict drain current and charges for a 3nm nanosheet transistor, then embed them in a standard cell library characterization flow spanning thousands of SPICE simulations, comparing accuracy, runtime, and convergence against Verilog-A-based BSIM-CMG.
result: The NN models achieve sub-0.11% delay error and 0.76% total power error across a wide range of circuits while being up to 8x faster in library characterization, and the paper further maps NN size to simulation precision.
conclusion: NN-based transistor models are a viable, faster alternative to conventional compact models for EDA flows, with practical guidance on accuracy-versus-size tradeoffs.

title: A Unified Variational Framework For Augmented Lagrangian Preconditioning Of Saddle Point Systems: Applications To Mixed-dimensional And Fictitious Domain Methods
authors: Michele Benzi, Marco Feder, Luca Heltai, Federica Mugnaioni
abstract: ArXiv:2610.30357v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a general framework to derive augmented Lagrangian preconditioners for saddle point systems arising from mixed finite element discretizations. Our approach is based on augmenting the variational formulation at the continuous level prior to discretization, providing a unified strategy for designing efficient preconditioners that are robust under mesh refinement for a broad class of problems leading to symmetric saddle point systems. The robustness of the proposed preconditioners is established through a detailed spectral analysis. This framework is applied to different model problems, focusing on mixed-dimensional and fictitious domain formulations involving Lagrange multipliers, with some configurations featuring large coefficient jumps. Extensive numerical experiments on different test cases and geometries are presented, validating the effectiveness and robustness of our preconditioners when used in conjunction with flexible GMRES.
tldr: A unified variational framework for constructing augmented Lagrangian preconditioners for saddle point systems arising in mixed finite element discretizations, applied to mixed-dimensional and fictitious domain methods.
motivation: Saddle point systems from mixed finite element formulations involving Lagrange multipliers are notoriously ill-conditioned and require preconditioners that remain robust under mesh refinement, especially with large coefficient jumps.
method: The authors augment the variational formulation at the continuous level before discretization, yielding a general recipe for block preconditioners, with robustness justified by detailed spectral analysis and tested via flexible GMRES on several model problems and geometries.
result: Spectral analysis establishes mesh-independent convergence behavior, and extensive numerical experiments on mixed-dimensional and fictitious domain test cases with large coefficient jumps confirm the effectiveness and robustness of the preconditioners.
conclusion: The framework provides a unified, principled strategy for designing robust augmented Lagrangian preconditioners across a broad class of symmetric saddle point problems, with practical validation in flexible GMRES solvers.

title: Robust Topology Optimization Of Isogeometric Kirchhoff--Love Shells By The Speed Method
authors: Philipp Eisenhardt, Fernando H\"ubner Scherer, Barbara Wohlmuth, Andrei Constantinescu
abstract: ArXiv:2610.30389v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper presents a framework for robust topology optimization of Kirchhoff-Love (KL) multi-patch shells using isogeometric analysis and non-matching meshes and provides a CAD-compatible method. The material distribution is optimized via a NURBS-based level set method, enabling accurate boundary representation and seamless export to standard CAD/CAM workflows. The shape derivative is computed using the speed method, yielding a volume-based formulation that avoids boundary approximations and aligns with the isogeometric principle of coarse, high-order discretizations. This eliminates the need for local refinement, adaptive quadrature, or trimming as the descent direction for the compliance and volume objectives are obtained through a biharmonic equation. The framework is extended to robust optimization under uncertainty, accounting for stochastic loading and material properties via Monte Carlo sampling and Gaussian Random Fields. Numerical examples demonstrate the method's efficiency and robustness across single- and multi-patch shells, reproducing literature results with fewer elements than traditional FEM or refined IGA approaches. The developed methods and tools can be directly extended to problems involving stress-based optimization and risk-averse metrics. The numerical implementations are open-source and available on GitHub.
tldr: This paper develops a CAD-compatible isogeometric framework for robust topology optimization of Kirchhoff-Love multi-patch shells using a NURBS level-set representation and the speed method for shape derivatives.
motivation: Topology optimization of shell structures typically requires trimmed geometries, local refinement, and adaptive quadrature, which complicates CAD integration and increases computational cost; the authors aim for a method free of these burdens that also handles uncertainty in loading and material properties.
method: The material distribution is optimized with a NURBS-based level-set method, with shape derivatives computed via the speed method yielding a volume-based formulation in which descent directions follow from a biharmonic equation; robustness is incorporated through Monte Carlo sampling and Gaussian random fields over stochastic loads and materials.
result: Numerical examples on single- and multi-patch shells reproduce literature benchmarks with fewer elements than traditional FEM or refined IGA approaches, while demonstrating efficiency and robustness under uncertainty.
conclusion: The approach offers an accurate, CAD-exportable, open-source workflow for shell topology optimization that can be extended to stress-based and risk-averse objectives.

title: When Evm Defaults Break: Three Sdk Patterns For UTXO-Family Wallets
authors: Hongzhou Chen Hanzheng Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2610.30183v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Mainstream Web3 SDKs (e.g., ethers.js, viem) bundle three coupled assumptions: an account-based ledger, a single secp256k1 signer, and input-selection-free transaction construction. These assumptions fail once a chain adopts an extended-UTXO model (here, the Cell model on Nervos CKB), and once the wallet population spans heterogeneous cryptographic primitives (secp256k1, WebAuthn, Schnorr). Using CKBers' Codebase (CCC), a TypeScript SDK, this retrospective case study extracts three recurring patterns from release history and exported APIs: a Transaction Composer that makes capacity-aware input completion and fee estimation declarative, a Unified Signer Abstraction that normalizes signing across heterogeneous wallets behind one interface, and a Connector UI component that ships per-wallet onboarding as a drop-in. The contribution is the articulation of these patterns as transferable design lessons for SDKs targeting UTXO-family ledgers and heterogeneous wallet populations.
tldr: A retrospective case study of the CKBers' Codebase TypeScript SDK that identifies three design patterns for building wallet SDKs on UTXO-family ledgers with heterogeneous signers.
motivation: Mainstream Web3 SDKs like ethers.js and viem assume an account-based ledger, a single secp256k1 signer, and input-selection-free transaction construction; these assumptions break on extended-UTXO chains such as Nervos CKB and with wallets spanning secp256k1, WebAuthn, and Schnorr.
method: The authors analyze release history and exported APIs of the CCC SDK to extract recurring architectural patterns: a declarative Transaction Composer for capacity-aware input completion and fee estimation, a Unified Signer Abstraction, and a drop-in Connector UI component.
result: The study articulates these three patterns as transferable design lessons for SDKs targeting UTXO-family ledgers and heterogeneous wallet populations.
conclusion: The work offers practical software-engineering guidance for blockchain wallet SDK design, with no connection to quantum information science.

title: Parameters Efficient Language Model With Latent Cross-attention For IoT Intrusion Detection
authors: Frederic Adjewa, Moez Esseghir, Leila Merghem-Boulahia, Cheikh Kacfah
abstract: ArXiv:2610.30222v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Language models have shown strong potential for intrusion detection, but their high memory and computational demands make them difficult to deploy in resource-constrained IoT environments. In this work, we propose a compact Transformer-based architecture that compresses the input into a small latent space before processing it with a minimal Transformer core. We analyze nine compression configurations, compare parameter sharing with layer stacking, and evaluate our approach against SecurityBERT on two IoT intrusion detection datasets, Edge-IIoTset and CICIoT2023. With only 306k non-embedding parameters and 1.6M parameters in total (6MB), our model is about 7x smaller than SecurityBERT (11.2M parameters, 45MB). With the same privacy-preserving encoding, it outperforms SecurityBERT by about 2 points of macro F1-score on Edge-IIoTset and is within 0.7 points on CICIoT2023. It is also about 89x faster on a simulated edge device. We further show that a single Transformer layer is sufficient, and that parameter sharing matches layer stacking with up to 66% fewer parameters. These findings show that lightweight Transformer-based architectures can provide a practical and accurate solution for intrusion detection in resource-constrained IoT settings.
tldr: The paper proposes a compact Transformer with latent cross-attention compression for resource-constrained IoT intrusion detection, achieving SecurityBERT-comparable accuracy with ~7x fewer parameters.
motivation: Language models perform well for intrusion detection but their memory and compute demands are prohibitive on IoT edge devices.
method: A Transformer-based architecture compresses inputs into a small latent space processed by a minimal Transformer core; nine compression configurations are analyzed and parameter sharing is compared with layer stacking, evaluated on Edge-IIoTset and CICIoT2023 against SecurityBERT.
result: With 306k non-embedding parameters (1.6M total, 6MB) the model is ~7x smaller than SecurityBERT, gains ~2 macro-F1 points on Edge-IIoTset, stays within 0.7 points on CICIoT2023, and runs ~89x faster on a simulated edge device; a single Transformer layer suffices.
conclusion: Lightweight Transformer architectures with latent compression offer a practical, accurate solution for IoT intrusion detection, though the work is entirely classical machine learning with no quantum information, thermodynamics, networking, or hybrid-systems content.

title: Mirage: Targeted Jailbreaks Against Post-Generation Safety Checkers In Multimodal Diffusion Models
authors: Shanghao Shi, Chaoyu Zhang, Heng Jin, Hao Li, Ning Zhang, Y. Thomas Hou, Wenjing Lou
abstract: ArXiv:2610.30348v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Post-generation safety checkers are widely employed in diffusion-model pipelines to prevent unsafe generated content from reaching users. In this paper, we show that these safety checkers can still be bypassed by our proposed multimodal jailbreak attack, Mirage. Given an adversarial target, which can be either a reference NSFW image or a malicious text description, Mirage conceals the target within an imperceptible perturbation applied to a benign input image. Mirage exploits the shared representation space of multimodal encoders to jointly align the perturbed image with the cross-modal adversarial target while repelling its representation from commonly filtered NSFW concepts. Such semantic separation can transfer across representation spaces, enabling Mirage to evade heterogeneous safety checkers without accessing their internal details. We further employ lightweight black-box query refinement to improve evasion near the unknown safety boundary. We implemented Mirage on Stable Diffusion 1.5, Stable Diffusion XL, and Kandinsky 2.2, and evaluated it on two cross-modal NSFW datasets, covering both text-to-image and image-to-image generation scenarios. The experimental results demonstrate that Mirage achieves strong targeted jailbreak performance across diverse post-generation safety checkers with limited black-box queries while preserving high semantic alignment with the adversarial targets.
tldr: Mirage is a multimodal adversarial jailbreak that hides NSFW or malicious targets in imperceptible perturbations to benign images, bypassing post-generation safety checkers in diffusion-model pipelines.
motivation: Post-generation safety checkers are widely deployed to filter unsafe diffusion-model outputs, but their robustness against adversarially crafted multimodal inputs is unclear and underexplored.
method: The attack exploits the shared representation space of multimodal encoders to jointly align a perturbed image with a cross-modal adversarial target while repelling its representation from commonly filtered NSFW concepts, supplemented by lightweight black-box query refinement to approach the unknown safety boundary.
result: Implemented on Stable Diffusion 1.5, XL, and Kandinsky 2.2 and evaluated on two cross-modal NSFW datasets across text-to-image and image-to-image settings, Mirage achieves strong targeted jailbreak success against heterogeneous checkers with limited queries while preserving semantic alignment with the targets.
conclusion: The results show that post-generation safety filters for diffusion models are vulnerable to transferable multimodal adversarial perturbations, implying that such defenses alone are insufficient and need adversarial-aware design.

title: Bridging The Closed-World Gap: Interpretable Anomaly Detection Via A Hybrid Tsk-fcm Ensemble On The Beth Dataset
authors: Lohith Srikanth Pentapalli, Josette Riep, Justin Ouwerkerk, Kelly Cohen
abstract: ArXiv:2610.30576v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A fundamental paradox plagues the deployment of Machine Learning in cybersecurity: supervised models generalize poorly to novel, Out-of-Distribution (OoD) attacks, whereas unsupervised models often suffer from poor separability, leading to unmanageable false-alarm rates. This challenge is exemplified by the BETH dataset, a kernel-level benchmark in which the training data consists solely of benign and suspicious insider behaviors, whereas the test set consists almost entirely of novel botnet activation attacks. To bridge this detection gap, we propose a Hybrid Fuzzy Ensemble that synergizes the precision of supervised learning with the adaptability of unsupervised clustering. Our architecture integrates a gradient-optimized Takagi-Sugeno-Kang (TSK) fuzzy classifier to act as an expert on known insider threats, with a parallel Fuzzy C-Means (FCM) module to detect geometric anomalies. A critical finding of our research is that traditional fuzzy membership scores degrade in high-dimensional feature spaces due to the curse of dimensionality. We overcome this by introducing a robust Min Distance metric that exploits the raw geometric isolation of botnet activation attacks. This approach yields a state-of-the-art AUROC of 0.9951 on the BETH test set, outperforming the original Isolation Forest baseline by 17.1%. By combining near-perfect OoD detection with the intrinsic interpretability of fuzzy logic, our framework offers a viable path toward robust, transparent, and autonomous network defense.
tldr: The paper proposes a hybrid fuzzy ensemble combining a TSK fuzzy classifier and Fuzzy C-Means clustering for interpretable anomaly detection on the BETH cybersecurity dataset.
motivation: Supervised models generalize poorly to novel out-of-distribution attacks, while unsupervised models often have poor separability and high false-alarm rates in cybersecurity settings.
method: The authors integrate a gradient-optimized Takagi-Sugeno-Kang fuzzy classifier for known insider threats with a parallel Fuzzy C-Means module for geometric anomaly detection, introducing a Min Distance metric to handle high-dimensional fuzzy membership degradation.
result: The hybrid framework achieves an AUROC of 0.9951 on the BETH test set, outperforming the Isolation Forest baseline by 17.1%.
conclusion: The approach offers robust, interpretable out-of-distribution attack detection for autonomous network defense, though it is unrelated to quantum information science.

title: Two-Timescale Antenna Positioning For Pinching-Antenna System Based On Statistical Channel Information
authors: Jingze Ding, Zijian Zhou, Bingli Jiao, Rui Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2610.30670v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper introduces a two-timescale antenna position optimization framework for the pinching-antenna system (PASS). The proposed framework exploits statistical channel state information (CSI) to determine large-timescale pinching-antenna (PA) positions over the entire waveguide, and utilizes instantaneous CSI to refine PA positions at the small timescale within a local region. This approach effectively captures the benefits of large-timescale PA positioning for long-term system performance and small-timescale PA movement for real-time adaptation to fast channel fluctuations. For the single-user case, we derive closed-form solutions for the optimal large-timescale PA positions, and further analyze a performance upper bound together with the conditions for achieving this bound, which guide the small-timescale position refinement. For the multi-user case, an upper bound on the minimum rate among all users is derived. To maximize their minimum rate, we develop an element-wise search algorithm for large-timescale PA positioning and a projected gradient ascent method for small-timescale position refinement. Simulation results show that the proposed scheme closely approaches the derived bounds and consistently outperforms conventional schemes by reducing path loss via large-timescale PA positioning and suppressing inter-user interference through small-timescale local movement.
tldr: A two-timescale pinching-antenna position optimization framework for wireless communication systems, using statistical CSI for large-timescale positioning and instantaneous CSI for small-timescale refinement.
motivation: Pinching-antenna systems (PASS) offer a new degree of freedom for wireless links, but antenna positions must adapt to both long-term channel statistics and fast fading, motivating a two-timescale design.
method: Closed-form large-timescale PA positions and an achievable-rate upper bound are derived for the single-user case; for multi-user minimum-rate maximization, an element-wise search for large-timescale positioning and projected gradient ascent for small-timescale refinement are proposed.
result: Simulations show the scheme approaches the derived bounds and outperforms conventional baselines by reducing path loss through large-timescale positioning and suppressing inter-user interference via small-timescale local movement.
conclusion: Two-timescale antenna positioning with statistical and instantaneous CSI is an effective strategy for PASS, though the work is entirely classical wireless-communication engineering.
